children.title: Exact Column-Generation Pricing
children.top_down_role: Column generation using globally accurate pricing information.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an optimal dual solution \((\pi,\sigma)\).
Every block pricing problem attains its minimum over \(P_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact pricing either supplies a negative-reduced-cost column or certifies full-master optimality when all block minima are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Exact minimum reduced cost in block k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact blockwise pricing for a minimization-form Dantzig-Wolfe master.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Solve the restricted master and obtain an optimal dual solution \((\pi,\sigma)\). For every block \(k\), compute exactly
\[
q_k=\min_{r\in P_k}\bigl(c_{kr}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{kr}-\sigma_k\bigr)
\]
and a minimizing column. If some \(q_k<0\), add one or more corresponding columns and resolve the restricted master. If \(q_k\ge0\) for every block, all omitted full-master dual inequalities hold, so the restricted-master primal solution is optimal for the full master. The algorithm stops under this latter condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact pricing globally minimizes each block's reduced cost. A negative minimum yields a column; nonnegative minima for every block certify full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Column-Generation Pricing

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

children.title: Inexact Column-Generation Pricing
children.top_down_role: Column generation using approximate, heuristic, or tolerance-limited pricing.

assumptions_latex: Each block pricing problem has finite optimal reduced cost \(q_k\).
The oracle tolerance satisfies \(\delta_k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned feasible column has reduced cost within additive error \(\delta_k\) of the exact pricing optimum.

notation.meaning: Exact minimum reduced cost for block k.
Reduced cost of the returned column.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses an additive-error oracle; multiplicative error is unsuitable when reduced costs cross zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An additive \(\delta_k\)-inexact pricing oracle for block \(k\) returns a feasible column \(\widehat r_k\in P_k\) whose reduced cost
\[
\widehat q_k=c_{k\widehat r_k}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{k\widehat r_k}-\sigma_k
\]
satisfies
\[
q_k\le \widehat q_k\le q_k+\delta_k,
\qquad
q_k=\min_{r\in P_k}\bigl(c_{kr}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{kr}-\sigma_k\bigr).
\]
The oracle may miss a negative-reduced-cost column when \(\widehat q_k\ge0\) but \(\delta_k>0\); therefore the returned column alone is not an exact termination certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact pricing returns a feasible column whose reduced cost is within a stated additive tolerance of the true block minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Column-Generation Pricing

children.title: Approximate-Pricing Certification
children.top_down_role: Certification issues arising when pricing information is not exact.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master is solved to primal-dual value \(z_R\).
For every block, a valid bound \(L_k\le q_k\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full-master optimum obeys \(z_R+\sum_k\min\{L_k,0\}\le z_F\le z_R\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on minimum block reduced cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive full-master objective certificate obtained by repairing block convexity dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\pi,\sigma)\) be an optimal restricted-master dual solution and let \(L_k\le q_k\) be certified for every block. Define \(\varepsilon_k=\max\{-L_k,0\}\) and \(\sigma'_k=\sigma_k-\varepsilon_k\). Then every full-master column satisfies
\[
c_{kr}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{kr}-\sigma'_k\ge0,
\]
so \((\pi,\sigma')\) is full-master dual feasible. Consequently,
\[
z_R-\sum_k\varepsilon_k
=z_R+\sum_k\min\{L_k,0\}
\le z_F\le z_R.
\]
Thus \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k\le\epsilon\) certifies an additive \(\epsilon\)-optimal restricted-master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified lower bounds on all block reduced-cost minima repair the master dual and yield an explicit additive optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Pricing Certification

children.title: Pricing-Accuracy Termination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on termination claims under incomplete or approximate pricing.

assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization LP and omitted columns may exist.
Termination uses only columns returned by an uncertified heuristic pricing routine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure to find a negative-reduced-cost column does not certify optimality without exact pricing or valid lower bounds on every omitted block minimum.

notation.meaning: Current restricted and full column sets.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp counterexample to termination based solely on an unsuccessful heuristic pricing call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider one convexity block with two columns having identical master coefficient \(1\), restricted set \(R=\{r_0\}\), full set \(P=\{r_0,r_1\}\), and costs \(c_{r_0}=0\), \(c_{r_1}=-1\). The restricted master has value \(z_R=0\), whereas the full master has value \(z_F=-1\). A heuristic that examines only \(r_0\) reports no negative-reduced-cost column and would terminate incorrectly. Hence unsuccessful inexact search is insufficient; termination requires exact minima or certified lower bounds strong enough to bound every omitted column's reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic may overlook an improving omitted column. Therefore, finding none is not an optimality certificate unless pricing accuracy supplies valid global lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Accuracy Termination Boundary

children.title: Pricing-Schedule Variant Family
children.top_down_role: Variants distinguished by pricing breadth, scheduling, and concurrency.

children.title: Multi-Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes that return multiple improving columns per search.

assumptions_latex: Exact or certified pricing produces a finite candidate set \(C_k\subseteq P_k\) for each processed block.
Only columns with negative reduced cost are eligible for insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update inserts multiple distinct improving columns before the next restricted-master solve.

notation.meaning: Candidate columns returned for block k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch insertion variant of column generation with duplicate suppression.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After solving the restricted master, pricing generates finite candidate sets \(C_k\). For each block choose
\[
S_k\subseteq\{r\in C_k\setminus R_k: c_{kr}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{kr}-\sigma_k<0\},
\]
subject to a prescribed batch-size or diversity rule, and update \(R_k\leftarrow R_k\cup S_k\) simultaneously before resolving the master. Multi-column pricing requires \(\sum_k|S_k|>1\) whenever at least two eligible distinct columns are selected. Exact termination remains permissible only when pricing or certificates establish nonnegative minimum reduced cost in every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-column pricing inserts a batch of distinct negative-reduced-cost columns before resolving the restricted master, while retaining the usual certified termination test.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Column Pricing

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The batch-insertion algorithm is plausible and fits the leaf, but the cited general delayed-column-generation section does not specifically establish the multi-column selection rule or its stated variant semantics. A direct multi-column pricing source is required.

children.title: Partial Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes that search only selected portions of the candidate space.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(t\), only blocks in a scheduled subset \(I_t\) are priced.
Every block is priced infinitely often unless the algorithm has already obtained a valid certificate for that block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Partial pricing reduces each iteration's pricing workload, but global termination requires current certificates for all blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair block-subset scheduling for decomposed column generation.

source_refs.locator: 7. Partial Pricing p. 143

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), choose a subset \(I_t\subseteq K\), solve pricing only for \(k\in I_t\), add any selected negative-reduced-cost columns, and resolve the restricted master when columns were added. A fair schedule satisfies: for every block \(k\), either \(k\in I_t\) infinitely often or a still-valid certificate already bounds \(q_k\ge0\). The method may continue after a priced subset yields no column. It may terminate as optimal only after exact or certified tests establish \(q_k\ge0\) for every \(k\in K\) at the terminating dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial pricing examines only scheduled blocks per iteration. Fair scheduling prevents permanent neglect, and termination still requires valid reduced-cost certificates for every block.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Pricing

source_witnesses.locator: 7. Partial Pricing p. 143

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited partial-pricing section may concern simplex-variable scanning rather than decomposed block pricing. The infinite-fairness condition and current-dual global certification rule need a source directly supporting this column-generation interpretation.

children.title: Parallel Pricing
children.top_down_role: Concurrent execution of pricing searches across blocks or candidate partitions.

assumptions_latex: At a fixed restricted-master dual vector, block pricing problems are independent.
Each worker returns columns and any claimed bounds tagged with the dual vector used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent block pricing calls may execute concurrently, with their results merged before the next master update.

notation.meaning: Restricted-master dual vector at iteration t.
Pricing result returned for block k.
Current restricted column set for block k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel pricing at a common restricted-master dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After solving the restricted master at iteration \(t\), broadcast \(y^t=(\pi^t,\sigma^t)\) to block workers. Concurrently, worker \(k\) solves or approximates its block pricing problem and returns a finite result \(C_k^t\) tagged by \(y^t\). After all required workers finish, merge distinct eligible columns and set
\[
R_k^{t+1}=R_k^t\cup C_k^t.
\]
Then resolve the restricted master. Because all workers use the same dual vector, exact nonnegative block minima may be combined into a global termination certificate; bounds computed at different dual vectors are not combined without additional validity analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel pricing solves independent block subproblems concurrently at one master dual vector, merges returned columns, and combines only mutually compatible certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Pricing

children.title: Pricing-Schedule Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of search breadth, subproblem selection, and concurrent pricing activity.

assumptions_latex: Each pricing result records its generating dual vector and whether its reduced-cost bound is exact or certified.
The restricted master is resolved only after a declared synchronization event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordination policy accepts columns safely and permits termination only from certificates valid at the current dual vector for every block.

notation.meaning: Dual vector used to generate a pricing result.
Certified block reduced-cost lower bound at the current dual vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for combining partial, batched, and parallel pricing schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing schedule is coordinated when every returned column is feasible for its block, duplicate columns are removed before insertion, and each result is tagged by the dual vector \(y^{s(k)}\) at which it was generated. A column may be inserted even if stale, but its reduced cost must be recomputed at the current vector \(y^t\) before being classified as improving. Termination is allowed only if, for every block \(k\), an exact value or certified lower bound \(L_k(y^t)\ge0\) is valid at that same current vector. Fairness additionally requires every uncertified block to be scheduled again.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordination tags pricing results by dual iterate, recomputes stale reduced costs, removes duplicates, schedules uncertified blocks fairly, and terminates only with current global certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Schedule Coordination

children.title: Column-Generation Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Families designed to control unstable restricted-master dual information.

assumptions_latex: The restricted-master dual feasible set is nonempty.
A stabilization center and finite stabilization parameters are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A column-generation stabilization modifies dual selection or movement while preserving a defined route to the unstabilized master problem.

notation.meaning: Stabilized dual objective or admissible region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Umbrella definition covering box, penalty, proximal, and bundle-style dual stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A column-generation stabilization is a family of restricted-master modifications parameterized by a center \(\bar y\) and stabilization parameters that replaces unrestricted selection of an optimizer in \(D_R\) by optimization of a stabilized objective or over a stabilized region \(\Phi_{\bar y}\subseteq D_R\). The modification must specify how centers and parameters are updated, how pricing multipliers are extracted, and how stabilization is relaxed or otherwise corrected so that a terminal certificate applies to the original full master. Its purpose is to control large or oscillatory changes in dual information without changing the target full-master optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column-generation stabilization controls restricted-master dual movement around a center while retaining an explicit mechanism for certifying the original full master.
knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Stabilization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This umbrella definition combines box, penalty, proximal, and bundle-style stabilization through one region-or-objective description. A direct authoritative source is needed to validate that abstraction and the claimed route to certification of the original full master.

children.title: Dantzig-Wolfe Reliability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Pricing certificates, dual oscillation, degeneracy, tail-off, hard pricing, and weak-decomposition boundaries.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Pricing Certificates
children.top_down_role: Pricing-based evidence for the presence or absence of improving columns.

assumptions_latex: The full master is \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda\ge 0\}\).
The restricted master over \(J_R\subseteq J\) has an optimal primal-dual pair, with equality-constraint multiplier \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^R\) is optimal for the full master if the pricing minimum is nonnegative.

notation.meaning: dual multiplier for the master equality constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-pricing certificate for a minimization-form Dantzig-Wolfe master.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232
6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every full-master column \(j\in J\), define its reduced cost by \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\). Restricted-master optimality gives \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) for \(j\in J_R\). If an exact pricing oracle certifies \(\min_{j\in J}\bar c_j\ge 0\), then \(\pi\) satisfies every full-master dual inequality. Hence the restricted primal solution, extended by \(\lambda_j=0\) for \(j\notin J_R\), and \(\pi\) are feasible for the full primal and dual with equal objectives, certifying full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-master solution is globally optimal when exact pricing proves that every omitted column has nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Pricing Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232
6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Dual Oscillation
children.top_down_role: Instability of master dual prices across column-generation iterations.

assumptions_latex: At some restricted-master iteration the set of optimal dual solutions is a non-singleton face \(D^*\).
Pricing uses the dual solution selected by the restricted-master solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual iterates need not converge, even when every iterate is restricted-master optimal.

notation.meaning: optimal dual face of the restricted master
dual vector selected at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvergence mechanism caused by nonunique restricted-master dual optima.

source_refs.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(D^*\) contains distinct vectors \(\pi^-\) and \(\pi^+\), then the sequence \(\pi^{2k}=\pi^-\) and \(\pi^{2k+1}=\pi^+\) consists entirely of optimal restricted-master dual solutions but does not converge. Because a candidate column \(a_j\) has reduced cost \(c_j-(\pi^k)^{\mathsf T}a_j\), pricing rankings can alternate whenever \((\pi^+-\pi^-)^{\mathsf T}a_j\ne 0\). Thus restricted-master dual optimality alone neither selects a stable multiplier nor guarantees stable pricing signals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonunique optimal dual face permits optimal multipliers to alternate, causing unstable reduced costs despite unchanged restricted-master objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Dual Oscillation

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alternating-selection example is mathematically plausible, but the cited general Dantzig–Wolfe section does not establish that solver-generated iterates can realize this oscillation or support the pricing-instability boundary as stated. A source specifically addressing dual instability or oscillation in column generation is required.

children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Master Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degenerate restricted-master structure and its computational consequences.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master is represented in equality standard form \(Bz=b\), \(z\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted master is degenerate exactly when some basic feasible solution has a zero basic component.

notation.meaning: basic components associated with the basis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form degeneracy specialized to a Dantzig-Wolfe restricted master.

source_refs.locator: 3.6. Column geometry and the simplex method p. 119
6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a basis \(\mathcal B\), the associated basic solution is \(z_{\mathcal B}=B_{\mathcal B}^{-1}b\) and \(z_j=0\) for \(j\notin\mathcal B\). A feasible basis is degenerate when \((z_{\mathcal B})_i=0\) for at least one \(i\in\mathcal B\). A Dantzig-Wolfe restricted master is called degenerate when it admits such a basis. Consequently, distinct feasible bases may represent the same master point and objective value, so a basis change or newly admitted column need not produce strict primal improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Dantzig-Wolfe master is degenerate when a feasible basis contains a zero basic variable, allowing basis changes without primal improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Master Degeneracy

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6. Column geometry and the simplex method p. 119
6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

children.title: Column-Generation Tail-Off
children.top_down_role: Late-stage regimes with slow objective or bound improvement.

assumptions_latex: The restricted-master lower bounds satisfy \(L_k\uparrow v^*\) with \(L_k<v^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tail-off occurs when \(g_{k+1}/g_k\to 1\), where \(g_k=v^*-L_k\).

notation.meaning: restricted-master lower bound after iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic bound-progress definition for minimization column generation.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=v^*-L_k>0\). Column-generation tail-off is the regime in which \(g_k\to 0\) but \(g_{k+1}/g_k\to 1\). Equivalently, the relative improvement \((L_{k+1}-L_k)/(v^*-L_k)\) tends to zero. Thus the method continues to generate valid improving columns and converges in bound, yet it has no eventual uniform linear contraction \(g_{k+1}\le qg_k\) for any fixed \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tail-off means the master bound converges while each iteration closes an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the remaining gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Tail-Off

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a minimization column-generation master restricted to a subset of columns, the restricted-master optimum is ordinarily an upper bound, not the increasing lower bound used here. The cited delayed-column-generation section also does not specifically support the proposed asymptotic ratio as the definition of tail-off. The intended bound sequence and an authoritative source must be supplied.

children.title: Hard-Pricing Boundary
children.top_down_role: Decomposition regimes where the pricing subproblem dominates computational difficulty.

assumptions_latex: Pricing requires solving \(\min\{(c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X\}\) exactly.
The pricing input and polyhedron \(X\) are encoded with polynomial bit length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: NP-hard exact pricing makes an exact column-generation iteration NP-hard unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: subproblem feasible set whose points generate columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-complexity boundary for exact Dantzig-Wolfe pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact pricing certificate must either return \(x^*\in X\) minimizing \((c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x\) or certify that its minimum is nonnegative. Therefore any implementation of one exact column-generation iteration solves the pricing optimization problem. If this optimization problem is NP-hard for the represented family \(X\), then exact pricing, and hence an exact iteration containing it, is NP-hard under polynomial-time reductions. The decomposition does not yield a polynomial-time algorithm merely because the restricted master is small, unless additional tractable structure is available or \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When exact reduced-cost pricing is NP-hard, each exact column-generation iteration inherits that hardness despite a small restricted master.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Pricing Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hardness inheritance argument is reasonable, and complexity_bound is the correct kind, but an NP-hardness statement requires a source identifying the represented pricing family and reduction model. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Weak-Decomposition Boundary
children.top_down_role: Block structures whose master coordination yields limited practical advantage.

assumptions_latex: The Dantzig-Wolfe formulation has a single block \(X\) with no separable product representation.
Pricing optimizes a general linear objective over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without block separability, Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition need not reduce the scale of its principal oracle problem.

notation.meaning: pricing objective vector induced by master duals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary where pricing retains the original-scale polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a single-block formulation, every pricing call has the form \(\min\{q^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X\}\). If \(X\) has no product structure or specialized optimization oracle, this call retains all variables and constraints describing \(X\). In the limiting case where \(X\) is the original feasible polyhedron and there are no genuinely complicating constraints, pricing is an original-scale LP with a changed objective. Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation then changes the master representation but provides no separability-based reduction of the principal optimization task.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the pricing set does not decompose, pricing can remain an original-scale LP, so the reformulation offers no structural computational reduction.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Decomposition Boundary

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

children.title: Benders Decomposition LP Interface
children.top_down_role: Projection-oriented decomposition for dual block-angular structure and complicating variables.

children.title: Benders Master–Subproblem Geometry
children.top_down_role: The separation of complicating variables from conditionally independent residual LPs.

assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y+d^{\mathsf T}x:y\in Y,\ Wx\ge h-Ty,\ x\ge0\}\).
The residual subproblem is an LP for each fixed \(y\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original LP equals \(\min_{y\in Y}\{c^{\mathsf T}y+Q(y)\}\), with \(Q\) represented by dual affine functions and feasibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-form LP Benders decomposition with inequality recourse constraints.

source_refs.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(y\in Y\), define \(Q(y)=\min\{d^{\mathsf T}x:Wx\ge h-Ty,\ x\ge0\}\). Its dual feasible region is \(P=\{\pi\ge0:W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le d\}\), independent of \(y\), and duality gives \(Q(y)=\sup_{\pi\in P}\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\) whenever the subproblem is feasible with finite value. Thus \(y\) belongs to the master, while conditionally independent residual variables remain in subproblems; dual points generate epigraph inequalities and dual recession rays generate feasibility inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing the complicating variables leaves a residual LP whose dual expresses the recourse value as a supremum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Master–Subproblem Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

children.title: Benders Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and optimality certificate families generated from dual subproblem structure.

assumptions_latex: The subproblem and dual region \(P\) are those of the Benders geometry record.
The candidate master point is \(\bar y\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual points certify lower bounds on recourse; dual recession rays certify necessary feasibility inequalities.

notation.meaning: master epigraph variable for recourse cost
dual feasible point attaining the subproblem value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and feasibility cuts for the stated inequality-form subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the subproblem at \(\bar y\) is feasible and finite and \(\bar\pi\in P\) is dual optimal, then \(\theta\ge\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\) is a globally valid optimality cut and is tight at \(\bar y\). If the subproblem is infeasible, a Farkas certificate is a vector \(r\ge0\) satisfying \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\) and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar y)>0\). Every master point admitting a feasible subproblem must satisfy the feasibility cut \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\le0\), which excludes \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual optima generate recourse lower bounds, while Farkas rays generate inequalities excluding master points with infeasible subproblems.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Certificate Families

source_witnesses.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

children.title: Benders Aggregation-Stabilization Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Single-cut, multi-cut, disaggregated, and stabilized organizations.

children.title: Single-Cut Benders Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Benders organizations aggregating subproblem information into one cut per round.

assumptions_latex: The recourse function is \(Q(y)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(y)\), where \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_sp_s=1\).
At \(\bar y\), each feasible finite subproblem has a dual optimum \(\pi_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One weighted inequality provides a valid aggregate lower support for total recourse.

notation.meaning: single epigraph variable for total recourse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-cut aggregation for a weighted family of separable Benders subproblems.

source_refs.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q_s(y)=\min\{d_s^{\mathsf T}x_s:W_sx_s\ge h_s-T_sy,\ x_s\ge0\}\). For dual optima \(\pi_s\ge0\) satisfying \(W_s^{\mathsf T}\pi_s\le d_s\), weak duality gives \(Q_s(y)\ge\pi_s^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sy)\). Summing with weights yields the single Benders cut \[\theta\ge\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\pi_s^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sy).\] It is valid for \(\theta\ge Q(y)\) and is tight at \(\bar y\) when every selected \(\pi_s\) is optimal there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-cut Benders combines all subproblem dual supports into one weighted inequality for total recourse.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut Benders Aggregation

source_witnesses.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

children.title: Multi-Cut Benders Disaggregation
children.top_down_role: Benders organizations retaining separate cuts from multiple subproblem components.

assumptions_latex: The weighted separable recourse model and dual optima \(\pi_s\) are as in single-cut aggregation.
The master uses one epigraph variable \(\theta_s\) per subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Disaggregated cuts imply their aggregate cut and therefore give a no-weaker relaxation for the same dual information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-cut epigraph representation for weighted separable recourse.

source_refs.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multi-cut master represents total recourse by \(\sum_{s=1}^Sp_s\theta_s\) and adds, for every generated dual point, \[\theta_s\ge\pi_s^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sy),\qquad s=1,\ldots,S.\] Multiplying these inequalities by \(p_s\) and summing gives \(\sum_sp_s\theta_s\ge\sum_sp_s\pi_s^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sy)\), exactly the corresponding aggregate cut. Hence, after projection onto \((y,\sum_sp_s\theta_s)\), the multi-cut relaxation is contained in the single-cut relaxation generated from the same dual points, although it uses more master variables and rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate epigraph cuts imply the corresponding aggregate cut, producing a no-weaker but larger master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Cut Benders Disaggregation

source_witnesses.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

children.title: Stabilized Benders Masters
children.top_down_role: Master variants designed to moderate unstable or poorly localized master decisions.

assumptions_latex: Initial cuts define a valid lower model \(m_0(y)\le Q(y)\) on \(Y\).
The stabilization parameter satisfies \(\rho_k>0\), and each subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns an exact Benders solution when its certified upper-lower gap meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of an exact Benders cutting-plane master.

source_refs.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar y^0\in Y\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and valid model \(m_k\), compute \[y^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{y\in Y}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}y+m_k(y)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert y-\bar y^k\rVert_2^2\right\}.\] Solve the subproblem at \(y^{k+1}\), append every resulting valid optimality or feasibility cut to form \(m_{k+1}\), and update the center to an evaluated point with the best incumbent feasible objective. Stop when a valid incumbent upper bound \(U_k\) and the unstabilized master lower bound \(L_k=\min_{y\in Y}\{c^{\mathsf T}y+m_k(y)\}\) satisfy \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\); output the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilized master selects trials near a center, while exact cuts and an unstabilized bound retain the usual Benders stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Stabilized Benders Masters

source_witnesses.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general Benders section does not specifically support the proposed proximal stabilized-master algorithm or its center-update rule. Moreover, a gap at tolerance ε>0 certifies ε-optimality, not an exact optimum; exact optimality follows only at zero gap. A stabilization-specific source and corrected guarantee are required.

children.title: Aggregation–Stabilization Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions among cut granularity, master size, information strength, and stability.

assumptions_latex: Single-cut and multi-cut masters use the same generated dual information.
Stabilization changes trial-point selection but all retained Benders cuts remain globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Disaggregation strengthens the relaxation, while stabilization controls trial movement without weakening the retained certificate system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness-preserving structural tradeoff, excluding instance-dependent runtime claims.

source_refs.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For identical dual points, the \(S\) disaggregated inequalities imply the corresponding single aggregate inequality, so the multi-cut lower relaxation is no weaker after projection, but it adds up to \(S\) cut rows per iteration instead of one. A stabilization term or trust region alters the selected trial point but does not invalidate any globally valid Benders cut in \(m_k\). Consequently, aggregation trades relaxation strength for master size, whereas stabilization trades unrestricted master minimization for controlled trial movement; exact optimality remains certifiable when bounds are computed from the valid unstabilized cut model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-cuts strengthen the master at greater size; stabilization controls trial movement while valid cuts and unstabilized bounds preserve exact certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation–Stabilization Tradeoffs

source_witnesses.locator: 6.5. Stochastic programming and Benders decomposition p. 254

children.title: Lagrangian Price Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition obtained by pricing coupling restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(k,m,n_1,\ldots,n_k\in\mathbb{N}\), \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is a nonempty polyhedron, \(c_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The coupled primal LP is feasible and has finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_P=\sup_{\pi\in\mathbb{R}^m}\{-\pi^\top b+\sum_{i=1}^k\inf_{x_i\in P_i}(c_i+A_i^\top\pi)^\top x_i\}\).

notation.meaning: local feasible polyhedron of block i
price vector for the coupling equation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Price decomposition for a finite block-angular minimization LP with equality coupling.

source_refs.locator: 10. Lagrangian Duality p. 80
6. Large scale optimization p. 231

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k,m,n_1,\ldots,n_k\in\mathbb{N}\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) be a nonempty polyhedron, \(c_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), and \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). For the primal problem \(v_P=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^k c_i^\top x_i:\sum_{i=1}^k A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\in P_i\}\), dualizing only the coupling equation with \(\pi\in\mathbb{R}^m\) gives \[g(\pi)=-\pi^\top b+\sum_{i=1}^k\inf_{x_i\in P_i}(c_i+A_i^\top\pi)^\top x_i.\] Evaluation of \(g\) therefore separates by block. If the primal problem is feasible and has finite optimal value, finite-dimensional LP strong duality gives \[v_P=\sup_{\pi\in\mathbb{R}^m}g(\pi).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing the shared equality constraints separates the Lagrangian by blocks; when the coupled LP is feasible and has a finite optimum, maximizing the dual function recovers its value.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Price Decomposition

children.title: Resource-Directive Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Primal coordination through allocation of shared resources.

assumptions_latex: \(k,m,n_1,\ldots,n_k\in\mathbb{N}\), \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is a polyhedron, \(c_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
Coupling occurs only through \(\sum_{i=1}^k A_i x_i=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^k c_i^\top x_i:\sum_{i=1}^kA_ix_i=b,\ x_i\in P_i\}=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^k\phi_i(r_i):r_i\in R_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^kr_i=b\}\).

notation.meaning: set of resources attainable by block i
optimal value of block i at a prescribed attainable allocation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal resource allocation representation for equality-coupled block LPs.

source_refs.locator: 6. Large scale optimization p. 231

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k,m,n_1,\ldots,n_k\in\mathbb{N}\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) be a polyhedron, \(c_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), and \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Define the attainable resource set \(R_i=A_i(P_i)\) and, for \(r_i\in R_i\), define \[\phi_i(r_i)=\inf\{c_i^\top x_i:A_i x_i=r_i,\ x_i\in P_i\}.\] Then the equality-coupled block problem has the exact master representation \[\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\phi_i(r_i):r_i\in R_i\text{ for every }i,\ \sum_{i=1}^k r_i=b\right\}.\] A feasible resource directive \((r_i)_{i=1}^k\) coordinates independent block subproblems, while the master equation enforces conservation of the shared resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate an attainable share of the shared resource to each block, solve the independent block problems at those allocations, and minimize their total value subject to resource conservation.

children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe–Benders Duality
children.top_down_role: The structural correspondence between generator-based and projection-based decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe–Benders Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-dual correspondence between column generation and Benders cutting planes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a block-angular LP whose local polyhedra have finite generator descriptions. Dantzig–Wolfe substitution expresses each local vector as a convex combination of its extreme points plus a conic combination of its extreme rays, producing a master LP with generator columns. The dual of this master has one inequality for every such generator. Applying Benders projection to the ordinary LP dual produces exactly these generator-indexed inequalities as feasibility or optimality cuts. Consequently, under consistent primal-dual sign conventions, a priced Dantzig–Wolfe column corresponds to a violated Benders cut for the dual formulation, and the two complete masters have equal optimal values whenever finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column generation for a block-angular primal is the LP-dual counterpart of Benders cut generation for its dual; generators and cuts correspond.
assumptions_latex: Each local feasible set is a polyhedron with a finite extreme-point and extreme-ray description.
The primal-dual pair uses mutually consistent equality and inequality conventions.
The relevant complete master has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{DW}}=v_{\mathrm{Benders\ on\ dual}}\), with generator columns corresponding to dual cuts.

notation.meaning: optimal value of the complete Dantzig–Wolfe master
optimal value of the complete Benders master applied to the LP dual

children.title: Implicit Column Models
children.top_down_role: Formulations accessed through pricing rather than explicit column enumeration.

assumptions_latex: \(J\) is a finite index set, \(a_j\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(c_j\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The pricing oracle globally minimizes reduced cost over \(J\).
The restricted master and its restricted dual have an optimal primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a restricted-master primal-dual optimal pair has dual price \(y\) and \(\min_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^\top y)\geq0\), then its primal solution is optimal for the complete master LP.

notation.meaning: dual price vector for the master equations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite LPs whose potentially large column family is accessed by pricing.

source_refs.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite index set, let \(a_j\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(c_j\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(j\in J\), and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). An implicit column model is an LP \[\min\left\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda_j\geq0\text{ for every }j\in J\right\}\] in which \(J\) is not explicitly enumerated. Given a dual price \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), a pricing oracle returns an index attaining \(\min_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^\top y)\), or certifies that this minimum is nonnegative. If \(y\) and a feasible restricted-master solution form an optimal primal-dual pair for the restricted master, then a nonnegative global reduced-cost certificate establishes optimality for the complete master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit column LP accesses an unlisted finite column family through global reduced-cost pricing. A restricted-master primal-dual optimum is also optimal for the complete master when pricing certifies that every column has nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Column Models

children.title: Implicit Row Models

assumptions_latex: \(J\) is a finite index set, \(a_j\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\beta_j\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(j\in J\).
The separation oracle is exact over the complete indexed family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{j\in J}(a_j^\top\bar x-\beta_j)\leq0\) if and only if \(\bar x\in P\).

point submitted to the separation oracle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite LPs whose potentially large inequality family is accessed by separation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite index set, with \(a_j\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\beta_j\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(j\in J\). An implicit row model is an LP whose feasible region is \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_j^\top x\leq\beta_j\text{ for every }j\in J\},\] where \(J\) is not explicitly enumerated. Given \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), an exact separation oracle either returns \(j\in J\) such that \(a_j^\top\bar x>\beta_j\), or certifies that every indexed inequality holds. The latter certificate establishes \(\bar x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit row LP accesses an unlisted finite inequality family through exact separation, which returns a violated row or certifies feasibility against the complete family.

children.title: LP Extended Formulations

knowledge_statements.title: LP Extended Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted polyhedral descriptions whose projection equals the target polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedron. An LP extended formulation of \(P\) is a finite linear system \[Q=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+p}:Ex+Fz\leq g,\ Hx+Kz=h\}\] such that its projection onto the original variables is exactly \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists z\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ (x,z)\in Q\}.\] The auxiliary variables may expose block structure or permit a shorter description, but they do not change the represented feasible vectors in the original space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP extended formulation describes a lifted polyhedron in original and auxiliary variables whose projection onto the original variables is exactly the target polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a polyhedron.
The lifted system contains finitely many linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary variables in the lifted space
polyhedron defined by the extended formulation

children.title: Explicit Formulation Size
children.top_down_role: Row, column, and nonzero counts in directly materialized LP descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Formulation Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding size of a directly listed rational LP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational LP written explicitly as \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\leq b,\ Ex=d\}\), its explicit formulation size is the binary encoding length of its dimensions, relation symbols, and all rational entries of \((A,E,b,d,c)\). Under a sparse encoding, this length is bounded, up to fixed coding constants, by the index storage for nonzeros plus the binary lengths of their numerators and denominators. Merely counting rows, columns, or nonzeros is therefore a combinatorial proxy and is not the full bit size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit formulation size is the binary length of the fully listed rational LP data; row, column, and nonzero counts alone ignore coefficient encoding.
assumptions_latex: All LP coefficients are rational numbers.
The encoding convention represents sparse indices and rational numerators and denominators in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{size}_{\mathrm{exp}}(A,E,b,d,c)\) equals the binary encoding length of the explicitly stored formulation.

children.title: Extended Formulation Size
children.top_down_role: Description size after introducing auxiliary variables or lifted constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Formulation Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint count of a specified lifted LP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an extended formulation \[Q=\{(x,z):Ex+Fz\leq g,\ Hx+Kz=h\}\] of a polyhedron \(P\), the inequality size of this formulation is the number of scalar inequalities in \(Ex+Fz\leq g\); equations are excluded because they may be eliminated or represented according to a separately declared convention. Its bit size additionally counts the binary encoding of all rational coefficients and indices. This distinguishes the size of one chosen lift from extension complexity, which minimizes inequality size over all valid lifts of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The size of a chosen extended formulation counts its lifted inequalities under a fixed convention; bit size also counts encoded coefficients and indices.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a finite extended formulation of \(P\).
The inequality-count and coefficient-encoding conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{size}_{\leq}(Q)=\operatorname{rows}(E\;F)\).

notation.meaning: number of scalar inequalities in the chosen lift

children.title: Extension-Complexity Interface
children.top_down_role: Connections between practical LP representation choices and exact extension size.

knowledge_statements.title: Extension-Complexity Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Yannakakis factorization theorem for nonempty polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope with an irredundant facet description and vertex set, and let its slack matrix be \(S\), where \(S_{fv}\) is the slack of vertex \(v\) in facet inequality \(f\). If \(P\) is not a single point, then its linear extension complexity—the minimum number of inequalities in any LP extended formulation projecting to \(P\)—equals the nonnegative rank of \(S\): \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_+(S).\] Hence factorization lower bounds for \(S\) are formulation-size lower bounds, while nonnegative factorizations construct extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nontrivial polytope, minimum LP extension size equals the nonnegative rank of its slack matrix, connecting formulations to matrix factorizations.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polytope that is not a single point.
\(S\) is a facet-versus-vertex slack matrix of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_+(S)\).

notation.meaning: minimum number of inequalities in an extended formulation of P
minimum inner dimension of a nonnegative factorization of S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is appropriate for this interface leaf, and the stated nontrivial-polytope version is standard. Because this is a named factorization theorem whose exact equality depends on extension-size conventions and degenerate cases, it requires an authoritative theorem-level citation.

children.title: Compactness Lower-Bound Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on obtaining compact exact LP representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Compactness Lower-Bound Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-matrix lower bounds rule out compact exact LP lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((P_n)_{n\geq1}\) be a family of polytopes, and let \(S_n\) be a slack matrix of \(P_n\). If \(\operatorname{rank}_+(S_n)\geq 2^{\alpha n}\) for some constant \(\alpha>0\) and infinitely many \(n\), then every exact LP extended formulation of \(P_n\) has at least \(2^{\alpha n}\) inequalities for those \(n\). Therefore no polynomial-size exact LP lift of this family exists. This boundary concerns exact linear projections; it does not by itself exclude approximation, nonlinear formulations, or implicit optimization and separation algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exponential nonnegative-rank lower bound on slack matrices excludes polynomial-size exact LP extensions, but does not exclude approximations or implicit algorithms.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_n\) is a nonempty polytope.
For infinitely many \(n\), \(\operatorname{rank}_+(S_n)\geq2^{\alpha n}\) with \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P_n)\geq2^{\alpha n}\), so \((P_n)\) has no polynomial-size exact LP extended formulations.

notation.meaning: polytope family indexed by input scale

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the terminal container, and the implication from an exponential extension-complexity lower bound is correctly scoped to exact LP lifts. It nevertheless depends on the unsourced slack-matrix factorization theorem and has no direct citation.

children.title: Explicit Sparse-Matrix Storage

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Sparse-Matrix Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compressed row, compressed column, and dual-orientation sparse storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) with \(s=\operatorname{nnz}(A)\), compressed sparse row storage consists of a row-pointer array of length \(m+1\), together with \(s\) column indices and \(s\) values. Compressed sparse column storage analogously uses a column-pointer array of length \(n+1\), row indices, and values. Thus either orientation uses \(O(m+n+s)\) machine words, with one dimension's pointer term dominant. Storing both orientations supports direct row and column traversal at \(O(m+n+s)\) words but duplicates values or index mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressed row or column formats store a sparse LP matrix in linear space in its dimensions and nonzeros; hybrid storage supports both traversal directions.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has \(m\) rows, \(n\) columns, and \(s\) explicitly stored nonzeros.
Indices and numerical entries each occupy a bounded number of machine words.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{storage}(A)=O(m+n+\operatorname{nnz}(A))\) machine words.

children.title: Matrix-Free LP Access

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free LP Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle representation exposing matrix actions without storing matrix entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free representation of an LP with constraint operator \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) provides routines that evaluate \(Ax\) for arbitrary \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(A^\top y\) for arbitrary \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), without requiring explicit storage or enumeration of the entries of \(A\). The vectors defining objectives, right-hand sides, and bounds remain separately accessible. An algorithm is matrix-free relative to this representation when every dependence on \(A\) occurs through these operator actions and declared auxiliary oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free LP access supplies products with the constraint operator and its transpose without explicitly storing the matrix, while exposing vectors and bounds separately.
assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is linear.
Both forward and transpose operator actions are available exactly or to a declared numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is accessed through \(x\mapsto Ax\) and \(y\mapsto A^\top y\), not through an explicit entry array.

notation.meaning: transpose operator required for dual or adjoint computations

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Operator Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free representation of a structured LP constraint operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), structured operator access is an interface \(\mathcal O_A=(\operatorname{apply},\operatorname{applyT})\) satisfying \(\operatorname{apply}(x)=Ax\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\operatorname{applyT}(y)=A^Ty\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), without requiring explicit storage of \(A\). The implementation may evaluate network, block, Kronecker, or generated components, but must return the products of the represented matrix exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured operator interface computes exact products by the constraint matrix and its transpose without explicitly storing the matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is fixed.
Both interface operations are exact in the mathematical model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{apply}(x)=Ax\) and \(\operatorname{applyT}(y)=A^Ty\).

children.title: Presolve Reduction Families
children.top_down_role: Bound, redundancy, fixed-variable, duplicate-structure, and implied-information reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Reduction Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving presolve for bounded-form linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), repeatedly apply a locally verifiable reduction: substitute a fixed variable \(x_j=\ell_j=u_j\); remove a redundant row; merge duplicate or proportional rows or columns when the required consistency conditions hold; or tighten bounds using valid implied information. Each step records a reconstruction map \(R_k\) and any objective offset. Stop when no enabled rule applies or infeasibility is detected. Return the reduced LP, the composed reconstruction data, and either a reduction log or a verifiable contradiction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve repeatedly removes fixed or redundant structure and tightens implied bounds while recording everything needed to reconstruct an original-space result.
assumptions_latex: Every applied reduction has a checked equivalence condition or a valid infeasibility implication.
Bounds may lie in \(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an equivalent reduced LP with reconstruction data, or a certificate that the original LP is infeasible.

notation.meaning: reconstruction map associated with presolve step k

children.title: Matrix Scaling-Equilibration Family
children.top_down_role: Row, column, and diagonal transformations for numerical balance.

children.title: Row Scaling
children.top_down_role: Row-oriented transformations for improving numerical balance in large LP systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Row Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal scaling of LP constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), choose a diagonal matrix \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\) with \(d_i>0\), and replace the equality system by \((D_rA)x=D_rb\). Because \(D_r\) is nonsingular, the systems have exactly the same feasible \(x\). If \(y'\) is a multiplier for the scaled system, the corresponding original multiplier is \(y=D_ry'\), since \(A^Ty=(D_rA)^Ty'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying every constraint row and its right-hand side by a positive factor preserves primal feasibility and gives an explicit dual-variable conversion.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(D_r\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\iff D_rAx=D_rb\), with multiplier conversion \(y=D_ry'\).

notation.meaning: multiplier for the scaled equality system

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports LP row-scaling equivalence.

children.title: Column Scaling
children.top_down_role: Column-oriented transformations affecting variable magnitudes and solver numerics.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal change of primal-variable coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), choose \(D_c=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) with \(s_j>0\) and set \(x=D_cz\). The equivalent scaled LP is \(\min\{(D_cc)^Tz:(AD_c)z=b,\ D_c^{-1}\ell\le z\le D_c^{-1}u\}\), with infinite bounds retained. Feasible points correspond bijectively through \(x=D_cz\), and corresponding points have equal objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column scaling changes variable units through a positive diagonal substitution while preserving feasible points and objective values bijectively.
assumptions_latex: \(D_c\) is diagonal with strictly positive finite entries.
Bounds lie in \(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and scaled LPs correspond bijectively under \(x=D_cz\) and have equal optimal values.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports LP column-scaling equivalence.

children.title: Diagonal Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Diagonal balancing regimes for sparse LP matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target row and column norms under two-sided diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) be positive diagonal matrices, and set \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\). For prescribed positive targets \(\rho_i\) and \(\gamma_j\), exact \(p\)-norm diagonal equilibration means \(\|\widehat A_{i,:}\|_p=\rho_i\) for every nonzero row \(i\) and \(\|\widehat A_{:,j}\|_p=\gamma_j\) for every nonzero column \(j\). Approximate equilibration with tolerance \(\tau\ge1\) replaces these equalities by membership in \([\rho_i/\tau,\tau\rho_i]\) and \([\gamma_j/\tau,\tau\gamma_j]\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal equilibration chooses positive row and column scalings so all nonzero row and column norms meet prescribed targets, exactly or within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le p\le\infty\).
All prescribed targets are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\) satisfies the stated row- and column-norm target conditions.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the selected norm-equilibration definition.

children.title: Scaling Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where scaling provides limited benefit or introduces numerical distortion.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural defects that nonsingular diagonal scaling cannot remove.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any matrix \(A\) and nonsingular diagonal matrices \(D_r,D_c\), the scaled matrix \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\) has the same zero pattern and rank as \(A\). Consequently, a zero row cannot acquire a positive target row norm, a zero column cannot acquire a positive target column norm, and rank deficiency cannot be removed by diagonal scaling. Thus exact positive-target equilibration is impossible when a target is imposed on a structurally zero row or column, and scaling alone cannot repair rank deficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular diagonal scaling preserves zeros and rank, so it cannot normalize zero rows or columns or repair rank deficiency.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are nonsingular diagonal matrices of compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(D_rAD_c)=\operatorname{supp}(A)\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(D_rAD_c)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\).

notation.meaning: index set of nonzero entries of A

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports these invariants of diagonal scaling.

children.title: Automatic Structure Detection
children.top_down_role: Detection of components, blocks, borders, networks, and weak coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Structure Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-based detection of separable blocks and sparse coupling borders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the sparsity pattern of \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), construct the bipartite graph \(G=(R\cup C,E)\), where \((i,j)\in E\) exactly when \(A_{ij}\ne0\). Compute its connected components; after corresponding row and column permutations, distinct components yield independent diagonal blocks. Given a specified rule that selects coupling vertices \(S\subseteq R\cup C\), remove \(S\) and compute the components of \(G-S\). Return the permutations, component memberships, border set, and the number of edges having one endpoint in \(S\) and the other in \((R\cup C)\setminus S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build the row-column incidence graph, find components, and apply a specified coupling-vertex rule to expose blocks and borders.
assumptions_latex: Only the structural nonzero pattern of \(A\) is used.
A rule for selecting the candidate border set \(S\) is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned permutations expose the disconnected blocks of \(G-S\) and identify their coupling through \(S\).

children.title: Postsolve Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse application of presolve transformations with residual validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reduced solution or certificate \(w_K\) and a presolve log with reconstruction operators \(R_K,\ldots,R_1\), process the reductions in reverse order by setting \(w_{k-1}=R_k(w_k)\) using recorded substitutions, deleted-row data, bound changes, and objective offsets. Produce original-space primal and dual variables \((x,y)\), or an original-space infeasibility or unboundedness certificate. Accept the reconstruction only if the applicable original-model residuals, bound violations, complementarity conditions, and certificate inequalities satisfy prescribed tolerances; otherwise report postsolve failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve applies logged reconstruction operators in reverse order, reconstructs original variables or certificates, and validates them against the original model.
assumptions_latex: Each presolve reduction stores sufficient reconstruction data.
Validation tolerances are fixed before acceptance.

children.title: Sparse Revised-Simplex Architecture

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Revised-Simplex Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal revised simplex with sparse basis solves and refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a standard-form LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), initialize a feasible basis \(B=A_{:,\mathcal B}\). At each iteration solve \(B^Ty=c_{\mathcal B}\), price nonbasic columns by \(\bar c_j=c_j-A_{:,j}^Ty\), and stop if \(\bar c_j\ge0\) for every nonbasic \(j\). Otherwise select \(j\) with \(\bar c_j<0\), solve \(Bd=A_{:,j}\), apply the minimum-ratio test over indices with \(d_i>0\), pivot, and update the sparse basis factorization. If no \(d_i>0\), report primal unboundedness; refactorize when prescribed stability or fill thresholds are exceeded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparse revised simplex method prices with basis solves, pivots using a ratio test, and maintains an updated sparse basis factorization.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank and the initial basis is primal feasible.
Pivot selection handles degeneracy without changing the stated optimality test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns an optimal basis when \(\bar c_j\ge0\) for every nonbasic \(j\), or detects an unbounded improving direction.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of nonbasic variable j

children.title: Sparse Interior-Point Architecture

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Interior-Point Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse Newton systems for primal-dual iterations in standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(s=c-A^Ty>0\), \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\), \(r_p=Ax-b\), and let \(r_c\in\mathbb R^n\) denote the complementarity residual. A primal-dual Newton step satisfies \[\begin{bmatrix}A^T&0&I\\0&A&0\\0&S&X\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta y\\\Delta x\\\Delta s\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}r_d\\r_p\\r_c\end{bmatrix}.\] Eliminating \(\Delta s\) and \(\Delta x\) yields a normal equation whose coefficient matrix is \(ADA^T\), where \(D=XS^{-1}\). A sparse architecture may factor either formulation while reusing permutations and symbolic structure across iterations and updating numerical values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse primal-dual method solves either a dimensionally consistent augmented Newton system or its normal equations while reusing sparse symbolic structure.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(X=\operatorname{diag}(x)\) and \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s)\) have positive diagonals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented and normal-equation formulations determine the same Newton direction under the stated nonsingularity assumptions.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices of primal variables and dual slacks

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Matrix Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric permutation chosen before sparse elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a structurally symmetric sparsity pattern \(\mathcal S\) for a matrix \(M\) to be factored, form its undirected adjacency graph and choose a permutation \(P\) using an ordering rule such as minimum degree or nested dissection. Symbolically eliminate vertices in that order: when a vertex is eliminated, connect all pairs of its remaining neighbors. Return \(P\) and the resulting symbolic elimination structure. Numerical factorization is then applied to \(PMP^T\); the ordering objective is to reduce predicted fill or elimination work, subject to numerical pivoting constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse ordering permutes a matrix using its graph so symbolic elimination predicts less fill and factorization work.
assumptions_latex: The symbolic pattern \(\mathcal S\) is represented by an undirected graph.
Any required numerical pivoting may modify the symbolic prediction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a permutation \(P\) and symbolic elimination structure for \(PMP^T\).

notation.meaning: permutation matrix defining the elimination order

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjacency-graph representation of symbolic sparse elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the graph representation of a symmetric sparsity pattern and the graph operation corresponding to one Cholesky elimination step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric sparse matrix $M\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$, define an adjacency graph with vertices $1,\ldots,m$ and an edge $\{i,j\}$ for each off-diagonal structural nonzero $M_{ij}$. Eliminating row and column $i$ is represented by deleting vertex $i$ and adding every missing edge between distinct vertices in $N_G(i)$. The resulting graph represents the structural sparsity pattern of the remaining matrix, and the number of newly added edges is the symbolic fill-in generated at that step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent the symmetric matrix by a graph whose vertices index rows and columns and whose edges are its off-diagonal structural nonzeros. Eliminating a row and column deletes the corresponding vertex and connects every previously unconnected pair of its neighbors. The new graph represents the remaining symbolic sparsity pattern, and its newly added edges count that step's symbolic fill-in.
assumptions_latex: M\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\text{ is symmetric and sparse.}
i\in V(G)\text{ is eliminated at the current Cholesky step.}
\text{Structural sparsity is tracked, so exceptional numerical cancellation is not used to remove symbolic fill.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G'=(G-i)\cup\bigl\{\{u,v\}:u,v\in N_G(i),\ u\ne v\bigr\},\qquad |E(G')\setminus E(G-i)|\text{ equals the symbolic fill-in at this step.}

children.title: Factorization Fill Growth
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing new nonzeros during factorization.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Fill Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fill generated by graph elimination under a fixed ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_0=(V,E_0)\) be the undirected graph of a structurally symmetric matrix and fix an ordering \((v_1,\ldots,v_{|V|})\). At step \(k\), eliminating \(v_k\) adds the set \(F_k\) of missing edges between its currently uneliminated neighbors. The symbolic fill is \(F=\bigcup_{k=1}^{|V|}F_k\). Its absolute growth is \(|F|\), and its normalized edge-growth ratio is \((|E_0|+|F|)/|E_0|\) when \(E_0\ne\varnothing\). These quantities depend on the ordering and describe structural factor storage before numerical cancellations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination creates fill edges between remaining neighbors; the union of those added edges and its ratio quantify ordering-dependent structural storage growth.
assumptions_latex: The factorization uses the fixed symbolic ordering without additional numerical permutations.
Structural zeros are interpreted graph-theoretically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\bigcup_{k=1}^{|V|}F_k\) is precisely the set of symbolic fill edges generated by the fixed elimination ordering.

notation.meaning: fill edges added at elimination step k
union of all symbolic fill edges

children.title: Symbolic Factorization Structure

assumptions_latex: \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, and only its structural nonzero pattern is used.
\(\pi=(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\) is a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

Uneliminated neighbors of the step-k vertex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric graph-elimination form, ignoring cancellations caused by numerical values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_0\) have vertices \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and edge \(\{i,j\}\) exactly when \(i\ne j\) and \(S_{ij}\) is structurally nonzero. At step \(k\), let \(N_k\) be the uneliminated neighbors of \(v_k\) in \(G_{k-1}\); join every pair in \(N_k\), then eliminate \(v_k\), producing \(G_k\). For the permuted factorization \(P_\pi S P_\pi^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), the symbolic column associated with \(v_k\) contains its diagonal and one entry for every vertex in \(N_k\). Thus the elimination sequence, filled graphs, elimination tree, and symbolic storage pattern depend only on the initial pattern and \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating vertices in the chosen order makes each current neighbor set a clique. These fill edges determine the symbolic triangular-factor pattern and elimination tree independently of numerical values.

children.title: Ordering Quality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among preprocessing cost, fill reduction, parallelism, and memory use.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) has a symmetric structural pattern on \(n\) vertices.
Each candidate permutation \(\pi\) is evaluated under generic noncancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ordering selection is a multiobjective comparison of storage, arithmetic, and dependency depth rather than a single universal ranking.

notation.meaning: Number of later neighbors when the step-k vertex is eliminated.
Symbolic nonzero count of the triangular factor.

review_flags: Exact source for the ordering-quality metrics is absent from the supplied inventory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic symmetric factorization with storage, work, and parallel-depth objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordering \(\pi\), symbolic storage satisfies \(F(\pi)=n+\sum_{k=1}^n d_k(\pi)\), while a standard dense-update work proxy is \(W(\pi)=\sum_{k=1}^n(d_k(\pi)+1)^2\). Parallel dependency is represented separately by the elimination-tree height \(h(\pi)\). Given nonnegative weights \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\), one scalar quality model is \(Q_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}(\pi)=\alpha F(\pi)+\beta W(\pi)+\gamma h(\pi)\). An ordering \(\pi_1\) dominates \(\pi_2\) only if all three measures are no larger and at least one is smaller; otherwise their quality comparison depends on resource weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordering can reduce fill yet expose less parallelism, or conversely. Storage, arithmetic work, and elimination-tree height therefore form separate objectives whose importance depends on computational resources.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Quality Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the LP as \(\min_{x\geq0}\max_{y\in\mathbb{R}^m} c^{\mathsf T}x+y^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\). children.title: Diagonal Preconditioning

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
\(T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) are positive diagonal matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) and \(S\) define a valid diagonal primal-dual preconditioner when the scaled coupling has norm below one.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal metrics for primal-dual splitting of the LP constraint operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((T,S)\) is an admissible diagonal preconditioner for the primal-dual coupling \(A\) if \(T=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\succ0\), \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\succ0\), and \(\|S^{1/2}AT^{1/2}\|_2<1\). In the equality-form LP iteration, scalar steps are then replaced by \(y^{k+1}=y^k+S(A\bar x^k-b)\) and \(x^{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb{R}_+^n}^{T^{-1}}(x^k-T(c+A^{\mathsf T}y^{k+1}))\). Because \(T\) is diagonal, the metric projection remains componentwise and preserves sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal primal and dual step matrices precondition the constraint operator. Their scaled operator norm must remain below one, while the nonnegative projection stays componentwise.

children.title: Adaptive Primal–Dual Scaling
children.top_down_role: Dynamic scaling regimes that balance primal and dual progress.

assumptions_latex: Positive steps \(\tau_k,\sigma_k\) are used by a primal-dual first-order method.
Nonnegative residual measures \(p_k\) and \(d_k\) quantify primal and dual error on comparable normalized scales.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update changes the primal-dual step ratio while preserving the stability-relevant product.

notation.meaning: Normalized primal and dual residual measures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-balancing adaptation with invariant step-size product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\mu>1\), \(\gamma>1\), and initial steps satisfying \(\tau_0\sigma_0\|A\|_2^2<1\). After iteration \(k\), compute normalized residual measures \(p_k\) and \(d_k\). If \(p_k>\mu d_k\), set \((\tau_{k+1},\sigma_{k+1})=(\tau_k/\gamma,\gamma\sigma_k)\); if \(d_k>\mu p_k\), set \((\tau_{k+1},\sigma_{k+1})=(\gamma\tau_k,\sigma_k/\gamma)\); otherwise leave both steps unchanged. Each update preserves \(\tau_{k+1}\sigma_{k+1}=\tau_k\sigma_k\), so an initially valid product bound remains valid. Practical convergence claims additionally require consistent residual normalization and bounded or summably varying adaptations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual balancing enlarges the step on the side with smaller normalized error and shrinks the other step reciprocally. This changes their ratio but preserves the product stability bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Primal–Dual Scaling

children.title: First-Order Step Control
