assumptions_latex: \(A\) is fixed and \(0<\theta<1\).
A computable upper estimate \(L\geq\|A\|_2\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted steps satisfy the standard primal-dual coupling bound.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically covers first-order LP step control.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-based backtracking for scalar PDHG step sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given trial steps \(\tau>0\), \(\sigma>0\), a safety factor \(0<\theta<1\), and contraction \(0<\rho<1\), accept the trial pair when \(\tau\sigma L^2\leq\theta\). Otherwise replace the designated step, or both steps proportionally, by a contracted value and repeat until the inequality holds. The accepted pair obeys \(\tau\sigma\|A\|_2^2\leq\theta<1\). Run the primal-dual update with this pair, and stop only when the chosen feasibility and gap residuals meet their tolerances. If \(L\) changes, repeat the acceptance test before using enlarged steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking contracts trial step sizes until their product times a valid squared operator-norm estimate lies below a safety factor, ensuring the accepted primal-dual coupling bound.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Step Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the step-control leaf and the stated implication follows from the norm upper bound, but no cited source identifies this acceptance and contraction procedure as a first-order LP step-control mechanism.

children.title: Adaptation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where adaptive controls oscillate, stall, or lose robustness.

assumptions_latex: The simultaneous primal-dual gradient iteration is applied to the bilinear saddle function \(\phi(x,y)=axy\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsafeguarded step adaptation cannot stabilize this iteration because every positive step product gives spectral radius greater than one.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the concrete instability boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete instability of unsafeguarded simultaneous primal-dual gradient updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\max_y axy\), consider \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\tau ay^k\) and \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma ax^k\). The iteration matrix is \(H=\begin{pmatrix}1&-\tau a\\ \sigma a&1\end{pmatrix}\), whose eigenvalues are \(1\pm i|a|\sqrt{\tau\sigma}\). Hence \(\rho(H)=\sqrt{1+a^2\tau\sigma}>1\), and every nonzero initial state outside the stable null subspace grows rather than converges. Residual-ratio adaptation that merely changes positive \(\tau\) and \(\sigma\) cannot remove this mechanism; a splitting, extragradient, damping, or other stability safeguard is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a scalar bilinear saddle problem, simultaneous primal-dual gradient steps have spectral radius above one for every positive step product. Residual balancing alone therefore cannot guarantee stability.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is correct and the spectral-radius calculation is internally coherent, but the concrete bilinear instability example has no inspectable citation. The phrase about a stable null subspace also needs source-backed clarification because this matrix has no nonzero stable subspace.

children.title: First-Order Solution Recovery Interface
children.top_down_role: Restart mechanisms and interfaces for improving accuracy or recovering basis-oriented solutions.

children.title: First-Order Restart Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Restart families intended to restore productive first-order progress.

assumptions_latex: A base first-order LP method produces iterates and a nonnegative merit function \(E\).
Restart parameters satisfy \(0<q<1\) and \(N\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restart rule resets the algorithmic anchor only after certified merit reduction or a prescribed epoch limit.
review_flags: Restart merits and guarantees depend on the underlying first-order method.
No supplied locator identifies the stated restart mechanism.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Merit-triggered epoch restarts for first-order LP iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the first epoch at \(z^{(0)}=(x^0,y^0)\). During epoch \(r\), run the base method and maintain any averages required by its merit evaluation. At the first index \(k\leq N\) satisfying \(E(z^k)\leq qE(z^{(r)})\), restart by setting \(z^{(r+1)}=z^k\), discarding epoch-local momentum or averages, and reinitializing the base recurrence. If no such index occurs by \(N\), either restart from the epoch iterate having minimal recorded merit or terminate with stagnation; this choice must be fixed in advance. Stop when \(E\) meets the requested feasibility and optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver runs in epochs and resets its anchor, momentum, and local averages after sufficient merit reduction. An epoch cap supplies a defined stagnation response.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Restart Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the restart-mechanism leaf, but the merit function, reduction trigger, epoch cap, fallback choice, and any associated guarantee depend on the base method and are not supported by a cited locator.

children.title: First-Order Solution Polishing
children.top_down_role: Postprocessing interfaces for improving solution accuracy.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), with dual slack \(s=c+A^{\mathsf T}y\).
An approximate primal-dual point \((\hat x,\hat y,\hat s)\) and threshold \(\varepsilon>0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polishing accepts a reduced-system correction only when it improves residuals without violating the LP sign constraints beyond tolerance.

notation.meaning: Indices predicted active at the nonnegativity bound.

review_flags: The supplied primal-dual locators do not specify this active-set polishing interface.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set reduced-system polishing of an approximate LP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(Z=\{j:\hat x_j\leq\varepsilon\ \text{and}\ \hat s_j>\varepsilon\}\) and \(F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus Z\). Set \(x_Z=0\), solve a reduced primal correction \(A_Fx_F=b\), and compute a dual correction satisfying \(A_F^{\mathsf T}y+c_F=0\), using least-squares or rank-revealing solves when the systems are not square. Set \(s=c+A^{\mathsf T}y\). Accept the polished point only if \(x\geq-\varepsilon\), \(s\geq-\varepsilon\), and a prescribed norm of primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity residuals is smaller than at \((\hat x,\hat y,\hat s)\); otherwise retain the original point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polishing predicts bound-active variables, solves reduced primal and dual equations, and accepts the correction only if sign conditions hold and feasibility and complementarity residuals improve.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Solution Polishing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The active-set algorithm fits solution polishing, but no supplied locator supports this identification rule, the reduced primal-dual systems, or the stated acceptance test. Rank-deficient and inconsistent reduced systems make the exact interface source-dependent.

children.title: Basis Crossover
children.top_down_role: Transitions from first-order solutions to basis-oriented LP representations.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\), and the LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\).
\(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) has \(|B|=m\) and \(A_B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting basis is an exact, directly verifiable optimal basic solution certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate produced after crossover to a nonsingular primal basis.

source_refs.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\). Define \(x_N=0\), \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\), \(y=-A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\), and \(r_N=c_N+A_N^{\mathsf T}y\). If \(x_B\geq0\) and \(r_N\geq0\), then \(x\) is primal feasible, \((y,r)\) is dual feasible with \(r_B=0\), and complementarity holds. Consequently \(c^{\mathsf T}x=-b^{\mathsf T}y\), so \(x\) is an optimal basic feasible solution. A crossover procedure is successful when it identifies such a set \(B\) from the approximate first-order solution and verifies these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Crossover is certified by a nonsingular basis whose basic solution is nonnegative and whose nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative. These checks establish feasibility, complementarity, and optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Crossover

source_witnesses.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

children.title: Recovery Interface Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where polishing or crossover becomes unreliable or disproportionately costly.

assumptions_latex: Recovery uses only an approximate primal point and threshold-based activity information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimality and arbitrarily small residuals do not ensure unique active-set or basis recovery.
review_flags: No supplied locator documents this concrete nonunique-optimal-face example as a recovery boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonunique-optimal-face instability of active-set and basis recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every point on \(\{x\geq0:x_1+x_2=1\}\) is optimal, including \(\bar x=(1/2,1/2)\). For any threshold \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), neither variable is identified as active at \(\bar x\), although a basis for the single equality contains exactly one column. Hence primal feasibility, zero objective gap, and strict positivity of both components do not identify a unique crossover basis. Moreover, replacing the objective by \(\delta x_1\) selects \((0,1)\) when \(\delta>0\) and \((1,0)\) when \(\delta<0\), so arbitrarily small data perturbations can reverse the recovered basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP with a nonunique optimal face can have a continuum of optimal points and multiple valid bases. Tiny objective perturbations select different endpoints, so residual accuracy alone cannot guarantee stable basis recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Interface Failure Boundaries

children.title: First-Order LP Certificates
children.top_down_role: Approximate optimality, infeasibility, and unboundedness certification interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order LP Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based certificates for a standard-form primal-dual LP pair and normalized improving rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\). A first-order \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate is \((x,y,s)\) satisfying \(\|Ax-b\|\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\|A^Ty+s-c\|\leq\varepsilon_d\), \(x\geq-\varepsilon_p\mathbf1\), \(s\geq-\varepsilon_d\mathbf1\), and \(|c^Tx-b^Ty|\leq\varepsilon_g\). A normalized primal-infeasibility certificate is \(y\) with \(\|y\|=1\), \(A^Ty\geq-\varepsilon_d\mathbf1\), and \(b^Ty<-\varepsilon_g\). A normalized unboundedness certificate is \(d\) with \(\|d\|=1\), \(d\geq-\varepsilon_p\mathbf1\), \(\|Ad\|\leq\varepsilon_p\), and \(c^Td<-\varepsilon_g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small primal, dual, and gap residuals certify approximate optimality; normalized approximate Farkas or improving rays certify infeasibility or unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\geq0\), with fixed vector norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual tests provide independently checkable approximate LP status certificates.

source_refs.locator: 6. Large scale optimization p. 231

review_flags: tolerance and norm conventions should be aligned with the surrounding first-order solver interface

source_witnesses.locator: 6. Large scale optimization p. 231

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized approximate rays do not by themselves certify infeasibility or unboundedness. Allowing componentwise violations in the Farkas inequalities requires additional bounds linking those violations to all feasible points or a verified robust alternative. The cited large-scale-optimization locator is not sufficient to establish these particular approximate status tests.

children.title: Parallel Large-Scale LP Execution
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes enabled by sparse operators, independent blocks, and replicated computation.

children.title: Shared-Memory Sparse Execution
children.top_down_role: Multicore execution over explicitly stored sparse models.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Memory Sparse Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact row-partitioned sparse operator evaluation by threads sharing one address space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the row sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\) form a disjoint partition of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let thread \(q\) store or access the sparse submatrix \(A_{I_q,:}\). For any \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), threads independently compute \(z_{I_q}=A_{I_q,:}x\), yielding the exact shared vector \(z=Ax\). For a transpose product, each thread computes \(w^{(q)}=A_{I_q,:}^Ty_{I_q}\), followed by the reduction \(w=\sum_{q=1}^p w^{(q)}=A^Ty\). Concurrent writes must either address disjoint output entries or use a mathematically exact reduction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threads evaluate sparse row blocks concurrently; transpose products additionally require summing thread-local contributions.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is explicitly stored in a sparse format.
\(I_1,\ldots,I_p\) are pairwise disjoint and cover all rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parallel evaluations equal \(Ax\) and \(A^Ty\) in exact arithmetic.

notation.meaning: row indices assigned to thread q

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block sparse matrix-vector multiplication follows directly from row partitioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block identities are correct in exact arithmetic, but the record has no inspectable source for its shared-memory execution and reduction requirements. Because the leaf concerns an execution procedure, algorithm is also a better content kind than representation.

children.title: Accelerator-Oriented Operator Execution
children.top_down_role: Throughput-oriented execution of sparse and structured operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerator-Oriented Operator Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batched execution interface for LP iterations dominated by sparse or structured linear operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given device-resident operator data for \(A\), vectors \(x,y\), and a batch size \(k\), allocate output buffers and evaluate the required products \(Ax\) and \(A^Ty\) using parallel kernels over nonzeros or structured blocks. Fuse elementwise updates and projections whenever they share the same operands, and synchronize before any dependent reduction or stopping test. For batched vectors \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) and \(Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\), compute \(AX\) and \(A^TY\). Stop after the host or device residual test is satisfied, and return the final iterates and residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep operators and iterates on the accelerator, batch linear products, fuse compatible updates, and synchronize before dependent reductions or termination tests.
assumptions_latex: The LP iteration accesses \(A\) only through \(Ax\) and \(A^Ty\).
The accelerator implements the stated sparse or structured operator and reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each completed kernel sequence realizes the same operator products and update dependencies as the serial iteration.

notation.meaning: number of vectors processed as one batch

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operator batching and dependency synchronization are standard accelerator execution constructs
performance and reproducibility conventions require an accelerator-specific source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the accelerator-specific batching, fusion, synchronization, or equivalence claims. Fusion is valid only after checking data dependencies and update ordering, so the instruction to fuse whenever operands are shared is insufficient to guarantee the stated serial-equivalence conclusion.

children.title: Distributed Matrix-Free Execution
children.top_down_role: Partitioned operator execution for models exceeding single-machine resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Matrix-Free Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact partitioned evaluation of LP operators without globally materializing the matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the rows into \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\). Worker \(q\) implements an oracle for \(v\mapsto A_{I_q,:}v\) and its adjoint \(u\mapsto A_{I_q,:}^Tu\), without storing a global copy of \(A\). To evaluate \(Ax\), distribute the required components of \(x\), compute \(z_{I_q}=A_{I_q,:}x\), and concatenate the blocks. To evaluate \(A^Ty\), compute \(w^{(q)}=A_{I_q,:}^Ty_{I_q}\) and perform \(w=\sum_{q=1}^p w^{(q)}\). Global residual norms and objective values are obtained by associative reductions; termination occurs only after those reductions complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers apply local operator blocks; concatenation forms forward products, while collective sums form adjoint products and global stopping statistics.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\) partition the rows of \(A\).
Each local forward oracle has the stated adjoint oracle.
Required vector components and reductions are communicated reliably.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In exact arithmetic the distributed procedure returns \(Ax\), \(A^Ty\), and the corresponding global scalar reductions.

notation.meaning: operator block assigned to worker q

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact block decomposition follows from matrix linearity
matrix-free distributed execution and communication model need a dedicated source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward concatenation and adjoint summation identities are mathematically standard, but there is no source for the claimed distributed matrix-free execution interface, communication requirements, or global termination semantics.

children.title: Large-Scale Numerical Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scale-dependent phenomena degrading reliability or computational advantage.

children.title: Conditioning-Scaling Pathology Coupling
children.top_down_role: Poor numerical geometry affecting convergence and certification.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned LP Geometry
children.top_down_role: Numerical geometry associated with poor sensitivity and slow solver progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned LP Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation-based geometric conditioning of an LP data instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=(A,b,c)\) denote LP data in a fixed product norm, and let \(\Sigma\) be the set of data at which the relevant status or solution property is ill posed, such as the boundary between feasible and infeasible instances. Define \(\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)=\inf_{\tilde d\in\Sigma}\|d-\tilde d\|\) and the relative geometric condition number \(\kappa(d)=\|d\|/\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\), with \(\kappa(d)=+\infty\) when the distance is zero. The LP geometry is ill conditioned at level \(K\) when \(\kappa(d)\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP is geometrically ill conditioned when its normalized data lie close to a boundary where feasibility, boundedness, or solution behavior changes.
assumptions_latex: A norm on the LP data space is fixed.
The ill-posed set \(\Sigma\) is specified for the status or solution property under study.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large \(\kappa(d)\) means a small relative perturbation can reach an ill-posed instance.

notation.meaning: chosen set of ill-posed LP instances

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

review_flags: ill-posed set must be specialized when connected to a particular solver status

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition resembles a distance-to-ill-posedness condition number, but the cited general sensitivity chapter does not inspectably support this formulation. The relevant property and ill-posed set must be fixed precisely; the conclusion that the distance can be reached also requires an attainment condition such as closedness of the ill-posed set.

children.title: Scaling-Induced Distortion
children.top_down_role: Numerical distortions introduced or amplified by scaling transformations.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) and \(D_c\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are positive diagonal matrices.
Fixed norms are used for the original and scaled residual tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absolute stopping tolerances in scaled coordinates need not represent comparable residual errors in the original coordinates.
review_flags: the exact scaling identities have been made explicit for the selected standard form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of absolute residuals under positive diagonal row and column scaling.

source_refs.locator: Affine-Scaling Steps p. 128

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\). Define \(r_p=Ax-b\) and \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\). For positive diagonal matrices \(D_r\) and \(D_c\), set \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\), \(\widehat b=D_rb\), and \(\widehat c=D_cc\). With \(x=D_c\widehat x\), \(y=D_r\widehat y\), and \(\widehat s=D_cs\), the scaled residuals satisfy \(\widehat r_p=\widehat A\widehat x-\widehat b=D_rr_p\) and \(\widehat r_d=\widehat A^T\widehat y+\widehat s-\widehat c=D_cr_d\). Hence absolute residual norms are not invariant under diagonal scaling and can be magnified or suppressed by the selected diagonal factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistent diagonal scaling preserves the primal-dual LP correspondence but multiplies the primal and dual residual vectors by the row and column scaling matrices, so absolute residual tests are not scale invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Distortion

source_witnesses.locator: Affine-Scaling Steps p. 128

children.title: Residual Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Persistent disparities among residual components after numerical balancing.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware condition detecting domination of one LP residual channel over another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive normalizers \(\sigma_p,\sigma_d,\sigma_g\), define \(\rho_p=\|Ax-b\|/\sigma_p\), \(\rho_d=\|A^Ty+s-c\|/\sigma_d\), and \(\rho_g=|c^Tx-b^Ty|/\sigma_g\). Given \(\tau>1\), the iterate has residual imbalance when \(\max\{\rho_p,\rho_d,\rho_g\}>\tau\min\{\rho_p,\rho_d,\rho_g\}\), interpreting a positive value divided by zero as \(+\infty\). This predicate identifies an error channel that is more than a factor \(\tau\) larger than another after normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual imbalance occurs when normalized primal, dual, and gap errors differ by more than a prescribed multiplicative factor.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma_p,\sigma_d,\sigma_g>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed ratio is a complete scale-aware predicate for residual imbalance at threshold \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: normalized primal, dual, and gap residuals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized residual ratios give a direct mathematical imbalance predicate
normalizer and threshold conventions are solver-dependent and need a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed predicate is internally consistent as a chosen definition, including the zero-residual convention, but no source establishes these normalizers or the threshold convention as the intended residual-imbalance interface for this leaf.

children.title: Certificate Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Effects of numerical conditioning on reliable LP status certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation margin for a normalized Farkas infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasibility of \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), let \(y\) satisfy \(\|y\|_2=1\), \(A^Ty\geq0\), and \(b^Ty<0\). Define its strict certificate margin by \(\mu(y)=\min\{\min_i(A^Ty)_i,-b^Ty\}\). Under perturbations \(A+\Delta A\) and \(b+\Delta b\), the same \(y\) remains a strict infeasibility certificate whenever \(\|\Delta A^Ty\|_\infty<\mu(y)\) and \(|\Delta b^Ty|<\mu(y)\). Thus small \(\mu(y)\) makes certificate validity sensitive to data or numerical error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas certificate with a small strict margin can be invalidated by correspondingly small perturbations of the constraint data.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) is a normalized strict Farkas certificate.
Perturbations preserve the dimensions of \(A\) and \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The margin \(\mu(y)\) is a directly verifiable lower bound on perturbation robustness of the certificate.

source_refs.locator: 1. Sensitivity Analysis p. 109

review_flags: locator may support general sensitivity rather than this explicit certificate-margin bound

source_witnesses.locator: 1. Sensitivity Analysis p. 109

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbation inequalities give a valid sufficient robustness test when the defined margin is positive, but the assumptions call the certificate strict without explicitly requiring every component of \(A^Ty\) to be positive. The cited general sensitivity locator does not inspectably support this explicit certificate-margin bound.

children.title: Factorization Fill-Memory Wall
children.top_down_role: Loss of sparse-factorization scalability through fill and memory traffic.

children.title: Factorization Fill Growth
children.top_down_role: Loss of sparsity during numerical factorization.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Fill Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic fill generated when a sparse LP linear system is factorized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a sparse square matrix and let \(P,Q\) be permutation matrices. Suppose Gaussian elimination produces \(PKQ=LU\). A position is fill if its entry is structurally nonzero in \(L\) or \(U\) but the corresponding position was structurally zero in the permuted input. Define the fill count by \(f(P,Q)=\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(U)-n-\operatorname{nnz}(K)\), with the diagonal overlap subtracted by \(n\), and the fill-growth ratio by \(\phi(P,Q)=(\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(U)-n)/\operatorname{nnz}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fill growth measures the new structural nonzeros introduced into sparse triangular factors relative to the original matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) admits the stated pivoted factorization.
Structural nonzeros are counted independently of accidental numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantities \(f(P,Q)\) and \(\phi(P,Q)\) quantify absolute and relative factorization fill.

notation.meaning: number of structural nonzeros in a matrix
fill count for the selected ordering

children.title: Factor Memory Footprint
children.top_down_role: Storage demands created by sparse factor data structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor Memory Footprint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage model for sparse triangular factors and their metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_F=\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(U)-n\) be the number of stored factor entries after accounting for a shared diagonal. If every value uses \(b_v\) bytes, every stored index uses \(b_i\) bytes, and the sparse format stores \(N_I\) indices plus \(N_P\) pointers, then the factor footprint is \(M_F=b_vN_F+b_i(N_I+N_P)+M_{aux}\), where \(M_{aux}\) includes permutations, scaling, work arrays, and allocator overhead. Factorization exceeds a memory budget \(M\) whenever \(M_F>M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor memory equals storage for numerical entries, sparse indices, pointers, permutations, work arrays, and overhead.
assumptions_latex: The sparse factor storage format fixes \(N_I\) and \(N_P\).
All simultaneously resident auxiliary arrays are included in \(M_{aux}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(M_F>M\) is a verifiable factor-memory-wall condition.

children.title: Memory-Traffic Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Bandwidth and data-movement limits affecting factorization performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Traffic Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roofline-style bandwidth limitation for sparse factor operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sparse factor kernel, let \(F\) be its floating-point operation count and \(B\) the bytes transferred across the limiting memory interface. Its arithmetic intensity is \(I=F/B\). If peak compute throughput is \(P_{max}\) and sustainable memory bandwidth is \(W_{max}\), the roofline bound is \(P\leq\min\{P_{max},W_{max}I\}\). The kernel is memory-traffic limited when \(W_{max}I<P_{max}\); equivalently, its attainable throughput is bounded by data movement before the compute ceiling is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse factor kernel is bandwidth limited when its arithmetic intensity is too low to reach peak compute throughput.
assumptions_latex: \(F>0\) and \(B>0\) describe the same kernel execution.
\(W_{max}\) is sustainable bandwidth at the relevant memory level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(I<P_{max}/W_{max}\) characterizes the memory-traffic bottleneck in this model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed roofline inequality is the conventional compute-versus-bandwidth model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The roofline inequality and resulting bandwidth-limited condition are mathematically standard and the content kind fits, but the record supplies no inspectable computer-architecture or performance-model source.

children.title: Ordering Breakdown Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structures for which available orderings fail to control fill or memory demand.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource failure persisting across every admissible sparse elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi\) be the admissible set of row and column orderings for a sparse system \(K\). For each \(\pi\in\Pi\), let \(M_F(\pi)\) be the predicted factor footprint and \(T_F(\pi)\) the predicted factorization work or time. Given limits \(M_{max}\) and \(T_{max}\), the ordering regime breaks down if \(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}M_F(\pi)>M_{max}\) or \(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}T_F(\pi)>T_{max}\). In that regime no admissible reordering alone can make the direct factorization satisfy the corresponding resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordering breaks down when even the best admissible permutation cannot keep factor memory or factorization cost within its resource limit.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\neq\varnothing\) is the fixed class of admissible permutations.
Resource predictions use one consistent factorization and hardware model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Crossing either infimum boundary proves that reordering alone cannot remove the specified factorization bottleneck.

notation.meaning: factorization resource cost under ordering pi

source_refs.locator: 1. Solving Systems of Equations: \( {LU} \) -Factorization p. 124

review_flags: ordering-specific fill and complexity support may require a sparse-direct-method source

source_witnesses.locator: 1. Solving Systems of Equations: \( {LU} \) -Factorization p. 124

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a finite admissible permutation family, the infimum boundaries are valid sufficient failure conditions and failure_boundary is the correct content kind. The cited generic LU locator does not inspectably support ordering-specific fill, memory, or time models, so a sparse-direct-method source is required.

children.title: Accuracy-Certificate Stagnation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Slow high-accuracy progress and weak recovery of reliable status certificates.

children.title: High-Accuracy Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Regimes where first-order progress slows sharply near stringent accuracy targets.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Accuracy Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision termination boundary for a primal-dual LP iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the LP pair 
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\},\]
define 
\[\eta_k=\max\!\left\{\frac{\|Ax_k-b\|}{1+\|b\|},\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y_k+s_k-c\|}{1+\|c\|},\frac{|c^{\mathsf T}x_k-b^{\mathsf T}y_k|}{1+|c^{\mathsf T}x_k|+|b^{\mathsf T}y_k|}\right\}.\]
High-accuracy stagnation occurs at level \(\tau>0\) when \(\eta_k>\tau\) eventually, while further iterations and stricter requested tolerances fail to produce a sustained decrease in \(\eta_k\). Thus the computed sequence cannot supply the requested accuracy certificate, even if its objective values appear stable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: High-accuracy stagnation occurs when normalized feasibility and duality-gap errors stop decreasing above the requested tolerance, despite continued iterations or stricter solver settings.
assumptions_latex: The iterates \((x_k,y_k,s_k)\) are represented in finite precision.
Residuals and gaps are evaluated using a fixed norm and scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The requested certificate \(\eta_k\le\tau\) is not obtained by the stagnating sequence.

notation.meaning: maximum normalized primal residual, dual residual, and duality gap

review_flags: Exact finite-precision stagnation criterion lacks a directly supporting supplied locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the displayed criterion is internally coherent, but no source supports this particular finite-precision stagnation definition or its scaling. The dimensions and domains of A, b, c, x_k, y_k, and s_k are also not introduced explicitly. A solver-numerics source with a section or page locator is required before the mathematical formulation can be relied upon.

children.title: Residual Plateau Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistent residual levels that resist further first-order reduction.

assumptions_latex: The residual sequence \((r_k)\) uses one fixed normalization.
The plateau-detection window has integer length \(w\ge 2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residuals remain above \(\tau\) without material improvement over the specified window or converge to a positive residual floor.

notation.meaning: allowed relative variation within the window

review_flags: Operational threshold convention is solver-dependent and requires a supporting source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational condition identifying a persistent numerical residual floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((r_k)_{k\ge 0}\) be a sequence of nonnegative normalized residuals, let \(w\in\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(w\ge 2\), and let \(\delta\in[0,1)\) and \(\tau>0\). For an index \(k\ge w-1\), a residual plateau above tolerance is present on indices \(k-w+1,\ldots,k\) when
\[\min_{k-w+1\le j\le k}r_j>\tau\quad\text{and}\quad \frac{\max_{k-w+1\le j\le k}r_j-\min_{k-w+1\le j\le k}r_j}{\max_{k-w+1\le j\le k}r_j}\le\delta.\]
An asymptotic plateau at level \(\rho>0\) is the stronger condition \(r_k\to\rho\). Either condition distinguishes failure to attain the tolerance from convergence for which \(r_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual plateau is a window of at least two nearly unchanged normalized residuals lying above tolerance; asymptotically, it is convergence of the residual to a positive floor.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Plateau Regimes

children.title: Status Certificate Weakness
children.top_down_role: Insufficiently reliable evidence for optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Status Certificate Weakness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a solver status label from a verifiable LP certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a claimed optimal solution of 
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\]
a mathematically checkable certificate consists of \((x,y,s)\) satisfying \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(x,s\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\). A status report is weak when it supplies only approximate residual bounds, omits the candidate vectors or scaling map, or uses undocumented tolerances. Such a report does not by itself certify exact optimality. Analogously, claims of infeasibility or unboundedness are weak unless accompanied by a verifiable Farkas or improving-ray certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver label is not an exact certificate when its vectors, scaling, tolerances, or residual checks are unavailable; infeasibility and unboundedness likewise require witnesses.
assumptions_latex: The LP data are available exactly or at accuracy sufficient for independent residual evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A status label alone does not imply a verifiable exact claim of optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.

notation.meaning: primal solution, dual multiplier, and dual slack

review_flags: Standard LP certification claim lacks a directly supporting supplied locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, and the optimality portion states the standard primal-dual checks. However, no source locator is supplied, the dimensions of the LP data are not introduced, and the Farkas and improving-ray certificates invoked for the other statuses are not specified. An authoritative LP certification source is needed.

children.title: Certificate Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of postprocessing intended to recover dependable LP status evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between recoverable approximate solutions and independently verifiable exact certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume rational LP data and an approximate primal-dual point \((\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)\). Certificate recovery succeeds only if a discrete candidate structure can be identified—such as a basis or rational vectors with prescribed denominator bounds—and the recovered objects pass exact checks. For an optimality claim, the recovered \((x,y,s)\) must satisfy 
\[Ax=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\qquad x\ge0,\qquad s\ge0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y.\]
Failure of rounding or rational reconstruction is not itself decisive; failure of every candidate to pass these exact equalities and inequalities marks the recovery boundary for the available approximation and bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate solution yields an exact certificate only after a basis or rational vectors are recovered and all primal, dual, sign, and objective checks pass exactly.
assumptions_latex: The LP coefficients are rational.
Exact arithmetic is available for final verification.
Any denominator or separation bound used in reconstruction is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful exact verification certifies optimality; without a verified recovered object, the approximation alone does not.
review_flags: Exact recovery conditions require a dedicated rational-certification source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The terminal container concerns a recovery boundary, so failure_boundary is more appropriate than certificate. More importantly, the candidate class, denominator bounds, separation conditions, and meaning of failure of every candidate are not specified sufficiently to establish a recovery theorem or boundary. A rational-reconstruction or exact-LP-certification source is required before a reliable replacement can be formulated.

children.title: Sparsity Without Useful Structure
children.top_down_role: Sparse models whose coupling, graph structure, or conditioning still prevents scalable solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Without Useful Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparsity alone does not guarantee decomposability, low fill, or favorable conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The bound \(\operatorname{nnz}(A)=O(n)\) does not imply that an LP with constraint matrix \(A\) admits independent blocks, bounded-fill factorizations, or uniformly conditioned linear systems. For example, matrices whose symmetric sparsity graph is an \(m\times m\) grid have \(n=m^2\) vertices and \(O(n)\) nonzeros, yet their graph is globally coupled and has separators of order \(\sqrt n\). Sparse elimination therefore creates nonlocal fill unless the ordering exploits separator structure. Independently, diagonal rescaling can preserve the zero pattern while making coefficient ratios and condition numbers arbitrarily large. Hence useful scalability requires structural and numerical properties beyond nonzero count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear nonzero count alone guarantees neither decomposition, low-fill factorization, nor good conditioning; grid coupling and extreme rescaling provide concrete failure mechanisms.
assumptions_latex: Sparsity is measured by the number of stored nonzero coefficients.
Direct factorization cost is governed by the associated elimination graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(\operatorname{nnz}(A)=O(n)\Rightarrow\) scalable numerical solution is false.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero entries of A
matrix dimension or number of graph vertices

source_refs.locator: 2. Exploiting Sparsity p. 127
6. Large scale optimization p. 231

review_flags: Grid-separator asymptotics should be checked against a sparse-factorization source.

source_witnesses.locator: 2. Exploiting Sparsity p. 127
6. Large scale optimization p. 231

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the topic, and the general conclusion that nonzero count alone does not ensure scalability is sound. The cited large-scale LP sections do not specifically establish the grid-separator asymptotics or resulting fill claim, and a constraint matrix may be rectangular, making its symmetric sparsity graph ambiguous without specifying a normal-equations, bipartite, or symmetrized graph. A sparse-factorization source with a precise locator is needed.

children.title: LP Relaxations of Mixed-Integer Models
children.top_down_role: The structural role of LP relaxations as continuous representations, bounds, certificates, and repeated subproblems in discrete optimization.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Integer Programming Formulations; Integer Programming Methods

children.title: LP Relaxation Construction
children.top_down_role: Principal ways continuous relaxations arise from mixed-integer models.

children.title: Integrality-Dropped Relaxation
children.top_down_role: The direct continuous relaxation of a mixed-integer formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Dropped Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct continuous relaxation obtained by replacing integrality declarations with continuous bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the mixed-integer feasible set be 
\[S=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb Z^q:A x+B z\le b,\ \ell\le(x,z)\le u\}.\]
Its integrality-dropped LP relaxation is 
\[P_{\mathrm{LP}}=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^{p+q}:A x+B z\le b,\ \ell\le(x,z)\le u\}.\]
Thus \(S\subseteq P_{\mathrm{LP}}\), and every linear inequality retained from the formulation remains enforced. For minimization with objective \(c^{\mathsf T}(x,z)\), whenever both optima are finite, 
\[\min_{(x,z)\in P_{\mathrm{LP}}}c^{\mathsf T}(x,z)\le\min_{(x,z)\in S}c^{\mathsf T}(x,z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct LP relaxation keeps all linear constraints and bounds but permits formerly integral variables to take continuous values, producing a valid minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: All displayed bounds and inequalities are linear.
The integer variables have continuous ambient domain \(\mathbb R^q\) after relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The containment \(S\subseteq P_{\mathrm{LP}}\) holds, giving the stated minimization bound.
review_flags: Standard definition, but no supplied locator directly addresses mixed-integer LP relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct content kind and the containment and minimization-bound direction are correct. Nevertheless, the record supplies no citation, and the dimensions and compatible domains of A, B, b, ell, u, and c are not explicitly declared. A mixed-integer optimization source with a specific relaxation definition locator is required.

children.title: Projection-Aggregation Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Relaxations obtained after eliminating or aggregating model structure.

children.title: Projected LP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: LP relaxations represented after eliminating selected model dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected LP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxations obtained by projecting a lifted polyhedron onto original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the target feasible set and let 
\[Q=\{(x,u)\in\mathbb R^{n+r}:Gx+Hu\le h\}\]
be a lifted polyhedron satisfying \(S\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). The projected LP relaxation defined by \(Q\) is 
\[P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists u\in\mathbb R^r,\ Gx+Hu\le h\}.\]
It is valid because \(S\subseteq P\). Optimizing a linear objective over \(P\) is equivalent in value to optimizing the same objective over \(Q\), since the auxiliary variables carry no objective coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected LP relaxation is the original-variable projection of a lifted polyhedron containing the target set; optimization can remain in the lifted variables.
assumptions_latex: The lifted set \(Q\) is a polyhedron.
Every point of \(S\) admits at least one feasible lift in \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\) is a valid polyhedral relaxation of \(S\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports projected or extended formulations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, and the projection and objective-value claims are mathematically standard. No source is supplied, however, and the row dimension and domains of G, H, and h are omitted. A source on projections or extended formulations with a specific definition or section locator is required.

children.title: Aggregated LP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: LP relaxations formed through grouped variables, constraints, or model components.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregated LP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxations formed from nonnegative combinations of existing inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a polyhedron \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) and a matrix \(T\in\mathbb R_+^{k\times m}\), the row-aggregated LP relaxation is 
\[P_T=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:TAx\le Tb\}.\]
Every point of \(P\) satisfies the aggregated inequalities because multiplication by the entrywise nonnegative matrix \(T\) preserves componentwise inequality. Consequently \(P\subseteq P_T\). Aggregation is exact precisely when the aggregated system implies every original inequality over the ambient domain; otherwise there exists \(\bar x\in P_T\setminus P\), and the aggregation strictly weakens the formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative combinations of original inequalities define an aggregated relaxation. It contains the original polyhedron and is exact only when it implies every discarded constraint.
assumptions_latex: The inequalities \(Ax\le b\) are interpreted componentwise.
The aggregation matrix satisfies \(T\ge0\) entrywise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The containment \(P\subseteq P_T\) holds; equality holds exactly when \(TAx\le Tb\) implies \(Ax\le b\).
review_flags: Standard aggregation definition lacks a directly supporting supplied locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, and nonnegative row aggregation gives the stated containment and equality criterion. The dimensions of A and b are only inferable from T, and no source locator supports the aggregation terminology or formulation. A precise polyhedral or aggregation reference is required.

children.title: Projection–Aggregation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparisons of relaxation size, strength, sparsity, and recoverability.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Aggregation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity, size, and strength relations for projection and row aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\) be a projected relaxation and let \(P_T\) be obtained from an inequality description of \(P\) using a nonnegative aggregation matrix. Then 
\[S\subseteq P\subseteq P_T.\]
Projection permits a small lifted description \(Q\) even when an explicit inequality description of \(P\) is large; eliminating the auxiliary variables may therefore increase representation size. Aggregation reduces the number of enforced rows from \(m\) to at most \(k\), but it cannot strengthen \(P\) and may enlarge it strictly. Thus compactness gained through aggregation is exchanged for possible relaxation loss, whereas lifting can preserve strength at the cost of auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection can hide a large original-space description behind auxiliary variables; aggregation reduces rows but can only preserve or weaken the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The aggregation matrix is entrywise nonnegative.
The projected formulation contains the target set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity and strength satisfy \(S\subseteq P\subseteq P_T\), while representation sizes need not follow the same ordering.
review_flags: The size-strength tradeoff needs a source on extended formulations and aggregation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is an appropriate content kind, and the containment S subset P subset P_T follows from the stated constructions. The representation-size and strength tradeoff is a nontrivial claim requiring a source on extended formulations and aggregation; none is supplied.

children.title: Structural Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where elimination or aggregation obscures useful model structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Witness conditions for strict weakening after projection simplification or aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq P\) and let \(R\) be a proposed simplified relaxation obtained by discarding projected coupling conditions or replacing inequalities by nonnegative aggregates. Validity is preserved when \(P\subseteq R\), but structural information is lost strictly exactly when 
\[R\setminus P\ne\varnothing.\]
A witness \(\bar x\in R\) with \(A_i\bar x>b_i\) for some original row proves strict loss under aggregation. For a lifted formulation \(Q\), a witness \(\bar x\) admitted by the simplified system but satisfying \(\nexists u\) with \((\bar x,u)\in Q\) proves loss of projected coupling. Any objective separating \(\bar x\) from \(P\) can then exhibit a strictly weaker relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural loss is strict when the simplified relaxation admits a point excluded by the original projection or a discarded row; that point is a verifiable witness.
assumptions_latex: The compared feasible regions are polyhedra in the same original-variable space.
The simplification preserves containment of the target feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A point in \(R\setminus P\) certifies strict structural loss and can be separated from \(P\) by a linear objective.
review_flags: Polyhedral witness statement is standard but lacks a directly supporting supplied locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, and a point in R minus P is the standard witness of strict enlargement. However, the class of projection simplifications is not defined precisely, and the separation/objective claim has no supporting polyhedral locator. A source is needed before accepting this boundary statement.

children.title: Extended LP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Continuous relaxations represented using additional variables or lifted structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended LP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted continuous formulation whose projection relaxes the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a target set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), an extended LP relaxation is a polyhedron 
\[Q=\{(x,u)\in\mathbb R^{n+r}:Gx+Hu\le h\}\]
such that 
\[S\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\{x:\exists u,\ (x,u)\in Q\}.\]
It is an extended formulation of a polyhedron \(P\) when equality \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\) holds. The formulation size is measured in the lifted space, commonly by its numbers of inequalities and variables; it may be smaller than every direct inequality description of the same projected polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended LP relaxation uses auxiliary variables and linear inequalities whose projection contains the target set; equality gives an extended formulation of that projection.
assumptions_latex: The target set lies in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
The lifted feasible region \(Q\) is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected set \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\) is a valid LP relaxation of \(S\).

notation.meaning: projection of Q onto original variables

review_flags: No supplied locator directly addresses extended formulations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct content kind, and the basic projection definition is sound. The assertion that a lifted formulation may be smaller than every direct description is an extension-complexity claim, not merely definitional, and requires authoritative support. No source locator is supplied.

children.title: Decomposition-Based LP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations represented through block convexification or generated columns.

assumptions_latex: The block index set \(I\) and all column index sets \(J_i\) are finite.
For every \(i\in I\), the set \(X_i\) is nonempty and bounded and \(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)=\operatorname{conv}\{v_{ij}:j\in J_i\}\).
The only cross-block constraints are the displayed linking equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master LP represents the relaxation obtained by replacing every block set \(X_i\) with \(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\).

notation.meaning: finite column index set for block i
vertex or column of the convex hull of block i
convex-combination weight for column j of block i
linear objective coefficient for block i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dantzig-Wolfe representation using convexified blocks and generated columns.

source_refs.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239
7.5 Block Diagonal or Angular Structure p. 361

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be a finite block index set. For each \(i\in I\), let \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and suppose
\[\operatorname{conv}(X_i)=\operatorname{conv}\{v_{ij}:j\in J_i\}\]
for a finite set \(J_i\). Consider the linearly coupled problem
\[\min\left\{\sum_{i\in I}c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\in X_i\ \text{for every }i\in I\right\}.\]
Replacing each block by its convex hull and writing
\[x_i=\sum_{j\in J_i}\lambda_{ij}v_{ij},\qquad \sum_{j\in J_i}\lambda_{ij}=1,\qquad \lambda_{ij}\ge0\]
gives the master LP
\[\min\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J_i}c_i^{\mathsf T}v_{ij}\lambda_{ij}\]
subject to
\[\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J_i}A_i v_{ij}\lambda_{ij}=b,\qquad \sum_{j\in J_i}\lambda_{ij}=1\ \text{for every }i\in I,\qquad \lambda_{ij}\ge0.\]
When the column sets are too large to enumerate, column generation represents this master LP implicitly and adds a column whose reduced cost, computed from the current master dual multipliers, is negative for this minimization formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposition-based LP relaxation replaces each block set by its convex hull, represents block points as convex combinations of columns, and couples those combinations in a master LP. Column generation can add negative-reduced-cost columns without enumerating all columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Based LP Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239
7.5 Block Diagonal or Angular Structure p. 361

children.title: Relaxation Strength-Geometry Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of continuous outer approximations of a discrete feasible set.

children.title: Ideal LP Formulations
children.top_down_role: The formulation family whose LP geometry coincides with the intended discrete hull.

assumptions_latex: The intended discrete feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is a polyhedron in original variables \(x\) and auxiliary variables \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(P)=\operatorname{conv}(X)\).

notation.meaning: Discrete feasible set represented by the formulation.
LP feasible region, possibly in an extended space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the projection-based definition, covering both original-space and extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set of a discrete optimization model and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be the feasible region of an LP formulation in variables \((x,z)\). The formulation is ideal with respect to \(x\) if
\[\operatorname{proj}_x(P)=\operatorname{conv}(X).\]
Equivalently, every linear objective depending only on \(x\) has the same optimal value over \(P\) as over \(X\), whenever that value is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP formulation is ideal when its projection onto the original variables equals the convex hull of all intended discrete solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Ideal LP Formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-based definition is mathematically precise and fits the ideal-formulation container, but no inspectable authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Dominance Between LP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Nested and incomparable relationships among alternative relaxations.

assumptions_latex: \(P_1,P_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) are LP relaxations of the same discrete feasible set \(X\), so \(X\subseteq P_1\cap P_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_1\) dominates \(P_2\) exactly when \(P_1\subseteq P_2\); they are incomparable when neither inclusion holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares relaxations in a common original-variable space by set inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(P_1,P_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(X\subseteq P_1\cap P_2\). The relaxation \(P_1\) dominates, or is at least as strong as, \(P_2\) if \(P_1\subseteq P_2\). It strictly dominates \(P_2\) if \(P_1\subsetneq P_2\). The relaxations are incomparable if \(P_1\nsubseteq P_2\) and \(P_2\nsubseteq P_1\). For minimization, dominance implies \(\inf_{P_2}c^Tx\leq\inf_{P_1}c^Tx\) for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation dominates another when its feasible region is contained in the other's; neither dominates when both contain points excluded by the other.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Between LP Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inclusion-based definition and minimization-bound implication are correct for relaxations in a common variable space, but the record has no citation.

children.title: Integrality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem families classified by the quality of their continuous bounds.

assumptions_latex: For each instance \(I\), \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)\) and \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\) are finite positive minimization optima with \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\leq z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family has gap factor \(\sup_I z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)/z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\), classified as exact, uniformly bounded, asymptotically vanishing, or unbounded as specified.

notation.meaning: Integer and LP relaxation optimal values for instance I.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses multiplicative gaps for positive minimization objectives; additive and maximization conventions require separate normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a family \(\mathcal I\) of minimization instances with \(0<z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\leq z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)<\infty\), define
\[g(I)=\frac{z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)}{z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)},\qquad g(\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}g(I).\]
The regime is exact if \(g(I)=1\) for every \(I\), uniformly bounded if \(g(\mathcal I)<\infty\), asymptotically vanishing along a specified sequence if \(g(I_k)\to1\), and unbounded if \(g(\mathcal I)=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrality-gap regimes classify instance families by whether the integer-to-LP optimum ratio is one, bounded, approaches one, or is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-minimization ratio convention is internally consistent and appropriately scoped, but the regime terminology and conventions require an authoritative source.

children.title: Symmetry-Degeneracy Pathology Family
children.top_down_role: Structural sources of weak bounds, redundant fractional structure, and unstable LP behavior.

children.title: Formulation Symmetry
children.top_down_role: Equivalent formulation structures that create redundant fractional representations.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the formulation region and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is its objective vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A group \(G\) is a formulation symmetry group when every \(g\in G\) preserves both \(P\) and the objective.

notation.meaning: Group acting linearly or affinely on variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines objective-preserving affine symmetries of an LP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be an LP feasible region with objective \(c^Tx\), and let \(G\) be a group of affine bijections of \(\mathbb{R}^n\). The group \(G\) is a formulation symmetry group if, for every \(g\in G\),
\[g(P)=P\quad\text{and}\quad c^Tg(x)=c^Tx\ \text{for every }x\in P.\]
Thus each orbit \(Gx=\{g(x):g\in G\}\) consists of feasible points having the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation symmetry is an invertible variable transformation that preserves the LP feasible region and objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Symmetry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-preserving affine-group definition fits the container and is internally consistent, but no inspectable symmetry source is supplied.

children.title: Primal Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degenerate primal geometry affecting LP movement and basis behavior.

assumptions_latex: The LP is written as \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A basic feasible solution is primal degenerate exactly when at least one of its basic variables equals zero.

notation.meaning: Basis index set with an invertible basis matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form, basis-dependent definition of primal degeneracy.

source_refs.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\). For a basis \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|B|=m\) and nonsingular \(A_B\), the associated basic solution satisfies
\[x_B=A_B^{-1}b,\qquad x_j=0\quad(j\notin B).\]
If this solution is feasible, it is primal degenerate with respect to \(B\) when \((x_B)_i=0\) for at least one \(i\in B\); otherwise it is nondegenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basic feasible solution is primal degenerate when one or more variables designated basic have value zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Degeneracy

source_witnesses.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

children.title: Dual Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degenerate dual geometry affecting multipliers and sensitivity information.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) of rank \(m\), and \(B\) is a primal-feasible basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis is dual degenerate exactly when some nonbasic reduced cost is zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses zero nonbasic reduced costs at a dual-feasible basis.

source_refs.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), let \(B\) be a basis and define
\[y=A_B^{-T}c_B,\qquad  ar c_j=c_j-a_j^Ty\quad(j
otin B).\]
If the basis is primal feasible and \( ar c_j\geq0\) for every \(j
otin B\), it is optimal. Such an optimal basis is dual degenerate when \( ar c_j=0\) for at least one nonbasic index \(j
otin B\); otherwise it is dual nondegenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal basis is dual degenerate when at least one nonbasic variable has zero reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Degeneracy

source_witnesses.locator: 11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

children.title: Symmetry-Induced Weakness
children.top_down_role: Weak bounds and unstable behavior attributable to symmetric formulation structure.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is convex, \(G\) is a finite formulation symmetry group, and \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The orbit average \(\bar x\) is feasible, symmetry-fixed, and has the same linear objective as \(x\), so distinct symmetric solutions may collapse to one fractional relaxation point.

notation.meaning: Average over the orbit of x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the orbit-averaging mechanism that can create central fractional LP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and invariant under a finite objective-preserving symmetry group \(G\). For any \(x\in P\), define
\[\bar x=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}g(x).\]
Then \(\bar x\in P\), \(h(\bar x)=\bar x\) for every \(h\in G\), and \(c^T\bar x=c^Tx\). If an orbit contains distinct integral points and \(\bar x\) is nonintegral, the LP relaxation admits a symmetry-fixed fractional point with their common objective value; symmetry alone therefore cannot distinguish those alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging distinct symmetric feasible solutions can produce an equally valued fractional point, exposing a mechanism by which symmetry weakens an LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Induced Weakness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Orbit averaging correctly produces a symmetry-fixed feasible point of equal objective value, but this point lies in the convex hull of the integral orbit and therefore does not by itself demonstrate a weak LP relaxation or an integrality gap. The claimed failure phenomenon is unsupported and does not fit the exact leaf sense.

children.title: Repeated LP Relaxation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: LP roles that recur inside mixed-integer search without reproducing the owning search algorithms.

children.title: Root-to-Node LP Relaxation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: The initial and locally restricted continuous subproblems used during search.

children.title: Root LP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Initial continuous subproblems used to establish global search information.

assumptions_latex: A mixed-integer minimization model has linear constraints \(Ax\geq b\), bounds \(\ell\leq x\leq u\), and designated integer coordinates \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root LP relaxation is obtained by dropping \(x_j\in\mathbb{Z}\) for \(j\in J\), and its optimum is a global lower bound on the mixed-integer optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the initial continuous relaxation before search-node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the mixed-integer minimization problem
\[\min\{c^Tx:Ax\geq b,\ \ell\leq x\leq u,\ x_j\in\mathbb Z\ (j\in J)\},\]
the root LP relaxation has feasible region
\[P_0=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\geq b,\ \ell\leq x\leq u\}.\]
If both optima are well defined, then \(\min_{x\in P_0}c^Tx\) is no greater than the mixed-integer optimum and is therefore a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The root LP relaxation drops all integrality restrictions before branching; for minimization, its optimum supplies a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Root LP Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and global lower-bound statement are correct for the stated minimization model, but no branch-and-bound source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Search-Node LP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Locally restricted continuous subproblems encountered during discrete search.

assumptions_latex: \(P_0\) is the root LP region, and search node \(v\) contributes valid local linear restrictions defining a polyhedron \(R_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node relaxation is \(P_v=P_0\cap R_v\), and its minimization optimum bounds every integer-feasible solution compatible with node \(v\).

notation.meaning: Restrictions accumulated on the path to node v.
LP feasible region at node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers branch restrictions and other valid node-local linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the root LP region. If node \(v\) accumulates branch decisions and other valid local linear restrictions represented by \(R_v\), its LP relaxation is
\[P_v=P_0\cap R_v.\]
Let \(X_v\) be the mixed-integer feasible points consistent with node \(v\). Validity requires \(X_v\subseteq P_v\). Hence, for minimization and nonempty \(X_v\),
\[\inf_{x\in P_v}c^Tx\leq\inf_{x\in X_v}c^Tx.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search-node LP adds the node's accumulated local restrictions to the root relaxation and bounds all integer solutions remaining at that node.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Node LP Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The node-relaxation construction and local lower-bound statement are mathematically sound and fit the container, but they lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Root-to-Node Relaxation Evolution
children.top_down_role: Changes in relaxation structure, bounds, and numerical behavior across the search tree.

assumptions_latex: Nodes \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_k\) lie on one root-to-descendant path, and every child inherits its parent's restrictions and may add valid constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{v_k}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq P_{v_1}\subseteq P_{v_0}\), so finite minimization LP bounds are nondecreasing down the path.

notation.meaning: LP region at search node v.
LP lower bound at node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumes inherited constraints; globally added cuts can strengthen all currently represented node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_k\) be a root-to-descendant path. If every child relaxation is formed by retaining all parent constraints and adding further valid restrictions, then
\[P_{v_k}\subseteq P_{v_{k-1}}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq P_{v_0}.\]
For a fixed minimization objective, define \(L_v=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in P_v\}\). Whenever these values are finite,
\[L_{v_0}\leq L_{v_1}\leq\cdots\leq L_{v_k}.\]
A descendant relaxation may also become empty, certifying that its search subtree contains no compatible feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inherited node restrictions make LP regions shrink down a search path, so minimization lower bounds cannot decrease and may culminate in infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-to-Node Relaxation Evolution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nested inherited relaxations yield nondecreasing minimization bounds as stated, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Local Restriction Effects
children.top_down_role: Effects of node-specific restrictions on feasibility, strength, and solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Restriction Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes validity within a search subtree from global validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_v\) be the integer-feasible solutions assigned to node \(v\), let \(P_0\) be the root LP region, and suppose \(X_v\subseteq P_0\cap R_v\). With \(P_v=P_0\cap R_v\), one has \(X_v\subseteq P_v\subseteq P_0\). Consequently, for minimization, whenever the displayed quantities are finite,
\[\inf_{x\in P_0}c^Tx\leq\inf_{x\in P_v}c^Tx\leq\inf_{x\in X_v}c^Tx.\]
If \(P_v=\varnothing\), then \(X_v=\varnothing\). The inclusion \(X\subseteq R_v\) for the global integer-feasible set \(X\) is not required, so a node-local restriction need not be valid outside the subtree rooted at \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrictions valid for the integer solutions assigned to a node shrink its LP relaxation, can strengthen its minimization bound or prove local infeasibility, and need not be valid elsewhere in the search tree.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the root LP region, \(X_v\) is the integer-feasible set assigned to node \(v\), and \(R_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(X_v\subseteq P_0\cap R_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(P_v=P_0\cap R_v\), local restrictions can improve the node bound or prove local infeasibility but need not be valid outside the subtree rooted at \(v\).

notation.meaning: Integer-feasible set assigned to node v.

children.title: LP Search Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Continuous certificates supporting bounding and exclusion decisions.

children.title: LP Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Continuous evidence supporting lower or upper bounds during discrete search.

knowledge_statements.title: LP Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasibility certificate for a minimization LP in inequality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal relaxation
\[\min\{c^Tx:Ax\geq b,\ x\geq0\},\]
any vector \(y\) satisfying \(y\geq0\) and \(A^Ty\leq c\) is an LP bound certificate with certified value \(b^Ty\). For every primal-feasible \(x\),
\[b^Ty\leq c^Tx.\]
Thus \(b^Ty\) is a lower bound on the LP optimum and on the optimum over any mixed-integer feasible set contained in the primal relaxation. The certificate is verified by checking \(y\geq0\), \(A^Ty\leq c\), and evaluating \(b^Ty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible vector certifies a computable lower bound on the minimization LP and on every mixed-integer feasible set contained in that relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The primal relaxation is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax\geq b,\ x\geq0\}\).
A vector \(y\) satisfies \(y\geq0\) and \(A^Ty\leq c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(b^Ty\) is a verifiable lower bound on every primal-feasible objective value and on any contained mixed-integer feasible set.

source_refs.locator: 6.1 Formulation of the Dual Problem p. 259
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

children.title: LP Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Continuous evidence supporting exclusion of infeasible search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: LP Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for an inequality-form LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). The system \(Ax\le b\), with \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \[y\ge 0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\] Such a vector \(y\) is an LP infeasibility certificate, verifiable from its sign, equality residual, and strict contradiction margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-form LP system is infeasible exactly when a nonnegative multiplier annihilates the constraint matrix and gives a strictly negative weighted right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
Certificate arithmetic is interpreted exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The existence of \(y\ge0\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) is equivalent to \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}=\varnothing\).
